questions.q: Q.1) Which one of the following organisms forms a unique symbiotic relationship involving a fungus and a photosynthetic partner, and has coevolved to an extent that neither partner can survive in the same way independently?
questions.e: Lichens represent an obligate and highly integrated symbiotic association between a fungus (mycobiont) and a photosynthetic partner (phycobiont). This relationship is so close that neither partner can survive in the same way on its own in harsh conditions.

questions.q: Q.2) Which of the following statements are correct with regard to the 'United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD)'? 1️⃣ It was adopted at the Rio Earth Summit in 1992. 2️⃣ It is the only legally binding international agreement linking environment, development, and sustainable land management. 3️⃣ It seeks to achieve Land Degradation Neutrality by 2030 as part of the Sustainable Development Goals. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The UNCCD was adopted in 1994 as a result of the 1992 Rio Earth Summit and is the only legally binding framework for sustainable land use. Its Strategic Framework (2018-2030) specifically targets Land Degradation Neutrality by 2030 in alignment with SDG 15.

questions.q: Q.3) Which of the following best describes the term 'mist netting', seen in news recently?
o: A fishing technique that uses fine nets in shallow coastal waters to trap small fish.
A wildlife research method in which fine nets are used to safely capture birds for scientific study.
A cyber security technique that uses decoy networks to trap and monitor malicious hackers.
A forest management practice used to control fog and mist in hilly plantation areas.
questions.e: Mist netting involves setting up nearly invisible fine nets to safely capture birds or bats for scientific research such as tagging or studying migration. However, it is increasingly being misused for the illegal hunting of migratory species.

questions.q: Q.4) With reference to the Bengal Tiger, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They have white spots on the back of the ears which function as 'false eyes'. 2️⃣ Unlike most mammals, they possess sweat glands all over their body. 3️⃣ They are known to use infrasound to communicate over long distances. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Bengal Tigers have white ear spots called ocelli that deter threats and aid communication. While they use infrasound for long-distance contact, they do not have sweat glands all over their body; like most mammals, these are limited primarily to their paw pads.

questions.q: Q.5) Consider the following statements with regard to Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZ): 1️⃣ The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 does not mention the word "Eco-Sensitive Zones". 2️⃣ The declaration of ESZs can extend up to 10 km from the boundary of a Protected Area. 3️⃣ All kinds of commercial activities in these zones are prohibited except agriculture. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: ESZs are notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, although the Act itself does not use the specific term. Guidelines suggest a 10 km extent, but they do not prohibit all commercial activities; instead, activities are categorized as prohibited, regulated, or permissible.

questions.q: Q.6) A carbon credit in India must meet which of the following conditions for trading in carbon market? 1️⃣ It must originate only from renewable energy projects. 2️⃣ It must be verified by an accredited agency. 3️⃣ It must be listed in the national carbon registry. 4️⃣ It must not arise from any legally mandated activities. 5️⃣ It must demonstrate long-term permanence of emission reductions. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: II, III, IV and V only
questions.e: Under India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme 2023, credits are not limited to renewable energy and can come from waste management or forestry. However, they must be verified by an accredited agency, listed in the national registry, meet additionality (not legally mandated), and ensure permanence.

questions.q: Q.7) Which of the following statements best describes the term 'Extinction Filtering'?
o: It is the natural reappearance of a species after a long period of extinction.
It refers to the extinction of a species due to lack of genetic variability in its population.
It refers to the survival of species that can withstand human disturbances.
It refers to selective protection of species based on conservation priorities in a managed ecosystem.
questions.e: Extinction filtering is a process where species sensitive to human activities disappear from degraded landscapes, leaving behind only those species capable of persisting despite habitat loss or fragmentation.

questions.q: Q.8) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Algal blooms can cause the sea water to appear red. Statement II: Euglenophytes produce a red pigment called astaxanthin. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is incorrect, but statement II is correct
Statement I is correct, but statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: Algal blooms can appear red due to the rapid accumulation of specific algae. Euglenophytes are one such group that produces astaxanthin, a red pigment that gives the water a striking red or pink color during a bloom.

questions.q: Q.9) With reference to the United Nations Ocean Conference 2025, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It was co-hosted by Brazil and Argentina. 2️⃣ It was held under the theme "Accelerating action and mobilizing all actors to conserve and sustainably use the ocean". 3️⃣ It witnessed the ratification of the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction Agreement by all United Nations member countries. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2025 UN Ocean Conference was co-hosted by France and Costa Rica in Nice. While the theme regarding accelerating action is correct, the BBNJ Agreement has not been ratified by all members; only 56 countries had ratified it by the time of the conference.

questions.q: Q.10) Consider the following information: 1️⃣ Cali Fund: To promote the conservation of Biodiversity - 16th Conference of Parties (COP16) to the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity. 2️⃣ Adaptation Fund: Finance adaptation projects for parties to the Kyoto Protocol - United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development, 2012. 3️⃣ Global Biodiversity Framework Fund: To help countries in the implementation of the Kigali Agreement - 16th Conference of the Parties (COP16) to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification. In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
questions.e: Only the Cali Fund is correctly matched, having been launched at the CBD COP16 to collect money from companies using genetic data. The Adaptation Fund was established in 2001 (not 2012), and the GBFF supports the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, not the Kigali Agreement.

questions.q: Q.11) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Biochar is a sustainable tool for soil improvement and environmental remediation. Statement II: Biochar has a porous structure and high surface area. Statement III: Biochar can be produced from agricultural residues through controlled pyrolysis. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
questions.e: Biochar is highly effective for soil remediation because it is produced via pyrolysis of organic waste, which results in a stable, porous structure with a high surface area. These physical properties allow it to retain nutrients and water effectively.

questions.q: Q.12) Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) that deals with the air quality management in National Capital Region (NCR) and Adjoining Areas was established under:
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
questions.e: The CAQM is a statutory body established under a specific piece of legislation: the Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas Act, 2021.

questions.q: Q.13) Which one of the following statements is not correct?
o: India ranks 3rd globally in terms of annual net gain in forest area.
India holds the 9th position in the world in terms of total forest area.
India ranks 1st globally in terms of forest carbon sequestration.
India, along with Indonesia, accounts for nearly 100% of Asia's agroforestry area.
questions.e: According to the FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment 2025, India ranks 5th (not 1st) globally in terms of forest carbon sequestration. It holds the 9th position in total forest area and 3rd in annual net forest gain.

questions.q: Q.14) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Its name is derived from a Sanskrit word meaning 'wood of the gods'. 2️⃣ It is a coniferous evergreen tree that thrives in cold temperate regions. 3️⃣ The wood of this tree is naturally resistant to rot, insects, and fungal decay. 4️⃣ It bears needle-like leaves and produces cones instead of flowers. The tree described above is:
questions.e: The Deodar (from Sanskrit 'Devadaru') is a Himalayan conifer known for its durable, rot-resistant wood. It is an evergreen tree with needle-like leaves and cones, traditionally used in temple construction and religious structures.

questions.q: Q.15) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Coral reefs have played a pivotal role in orchestrating Earth's climate rhythms for over 250 million years. Statement II: Coral reefs influence ocean alkalinity and regulate the ocean's ability to absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.e: Coral reefs regulate the Earth's climate by influencing ocean alkalinity through the removal of calcium carbonate. This chemical process dictates how much CO2 the ocean can absorb, thereby driving long-term climate phases over millions of years.

questions.q: Q.16) In order to achieve the 20% Ethanol blending target by the Ethanol Supply Year (ESY) 2025-26, which of the following feedstocks are permitted under India's biofuel policy for ethanol production? 1️⃣ Foodgrains unsuitable for human consumption 2️⃣ Sugarcane juice 3️⃣ Cotton stalk 4️⃣ Cassava Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: India's amended National Policy on Biofuels permits a wide range of feedstocks including damaged food grains, sugarcane juice, agricultural residues like cotton stalks, and starch-heavy plants like cassava to reach the 20% blending target.

questions.q: Q.17) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Chemical-solvent based carbon capture systems are preferred for coal-based thermal power plants. Statement II: Flue gas streams from coal-based thermal power plants have a very high carbon dioxide concentration. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: Chemical solvents are preferred for coal plants because they can effectively capture CO2 even from streams with low partial pressure. Statement II is incorrect because coal flue gas actually has a relatively low CO2 concentration (10-15%).

questions.q: Q.18) With reference to the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, in India, which one of the following statements is not correct? 1️⃣ The extended producer responsibility shall lie entirely on the producer only. 2️⃣ The quantity recycled is computed on the basis of end products. 3️⃣ EPR certificates can be traded on the Electronic Trading and Settlement Platform. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: All three statements provided are actually correct under the 2022 rules. EPR lies with producers, recycling is verified by end-products to prevent fraud, and a trading platform (EPRETP) exists for EPR certificates. Since the question asks which is "not correct," the answer is "None."

questions.q: Q.19) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Catchment degradation has led to worsening of flood peaks in India. Statement II: Loss of vegetation cover reduces interception and enhances the velocity of runoff water. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: Degradation of catchments through the loss of trees and plants prevents the natural "sponge" effect of forests. This leads to higher velocity surface runoff, which carries debris and sediment, resulting in more severe flood peaks.

questions.q: Q.20) Consider the following statements with regard to Project Elephant: 1️⃣ It is implemented only within designated Elephant Reserves. 2️⃣ It is merged with Project Tiger for budgetary allocation funding. 3️⃣ Notification of an Elephant Reserve under Project Elephant creates a legally protected area under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Project Elephant follows a landscape approach extending beyond designated reserves. In 2023, it was merged with Project Tiger for funding purposes. Unlike National Parks, Elephant Reserves themselves do not carry the same legal protection status under the 1972 Act.

questions.q: Q.21) Consider the following statements about the Climate Investment Funds (CIF): 1️⃣ It is the only global climate fund that works exclusively through six AAA-rated Multilateral Development Banks. 2️⃣ It is the first multilateral climate fund to list bonds on the capital markets. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The CIF provides large-scale climate finance specifically through six MDBs. It also made history as the first multilateral climate fund to utilize the capital markets by listing bonds to mobilize private investment.

questions.q: Q.22) Which of the following statements with regard to Green Ammonia is/are not correct? 1️⃣ The conversion of hydrogen to green ammonia requires nitrogen extracted from the air. 2️⃣ It has a high hydrogen density, making it an excellent carrier for transporting hydrogen. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Both statements are scientifically accurate descriptions of green ammonia. It uses nitrogen from the air and serves as an efficient liquid carrier for hydrogen. Since neither statement is "not correct," the answer is "Neither I nor II."

questions.q: Q.23) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Complete eradication of all invasive species is neither practical nor economically viable. Statement II: Most of the crops that dominate global agriculture are non-native. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
questions.e: Eradicating all non-native species would collapse global food systems because much of our agriculture depends on non-native crops. For instance, nine non-native crops comprise two-thirds of global production, making total eradication unfeasible.

questions.q: Q.24) Consider the following statements with regard to India's environment targets: 1️⃣ Restore 26 million hectares of degraded land is targeted by 2030 2️⃣ Derive 50 percent of cumulative electric power installed capacity from non-fossil fuel-based energy resources by 2030 3️⃣ Achieve 100 percent scientific processing of waste is targeted by 2026 4️⃣ Reduce the emissions intensity of GDP by half by 2050 Which of the above are India's environmental targets?
questions.e: India aims to restore 26 million hectares of land by 2030 and achieve 50% non-fossil electricity capacity by 2030. SBM-U 2.0 targets 100% waste processing by 2026. However, the GDP emission intensity target is a 45% reduction (not half) by 2030.

questions.q: Q.25) Which one of the following is the best description of the International Solar Alliance's 'Towards 1000' initiative?
o: It is a programme designed to install 1000 MW of rooftop solar systems in selected urban areas.
It is a global initiative aimed at mobilising 1 trillion US dollars to achieve 1000 GW of solar power capacity.
It is a scheme focused on setting up 1000 concentrated solar power plants in arid and semi-arid regions.
It is an initiative to standardise 1000 models of solar panels across India.
questions.e: The ISA's "Towards 1000" vision aims to mobilize $1 trillion in investments to install 1,000 GW of solar capacity by 2030, while also providing energy access to one billion people.

questions.q: Q.26) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Greenhouse gas concentrations in the Central Himalayas are generally higher than those at other remote background sites. Statement II: Monsoons and valley winds transport greenhouse gases from the Indo-Gangetic Plains to the Himalayas. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II is not the correct explanation for Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II is the correct explanation for Statement I
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
questions.e: Despite limited local industry, the Central Himalayas show high GHG levels because meteorological factors like monsoons and valley winds lift pollutants from the densely populated and industrial Indo-Gangetic Plain and trap them in the mountains.

questions.q: Q.27) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Arctic sea ice: Rising Arctic temperatures leading to albedo loss 2️⃣ Amazon rainforest: Declining moisture recycling and stronger dry seasons 3️⃣ Permafrost: Sustained increase in mean surface temperature 4️⃣ Coral reef systems: Ocean acidification caused by increased CO2 absorption How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The first three pairs are correct tipping point triggers. For coral reefs, while acidification is a stressor, the primary tipping trigger is actually marine heatwaves and rising sea surface temperatures leading to mass bleaching.

questions.q: Q.28) Consider the following statements about the particulate matters(PM): 1️⃣ PM10 tends to settle more rapidly in the atmosphere than PM2.5. 2️⃣ PM10 generally exerts a greater radiative forcing effect than PM2.5. 3️⃣ PM2.5 penetrates deeper into the lungs and bloodstream than PM10. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PM10 particles are heavier and settle faster due to gravity. However, PM2.5 has a greater radiative forcing effect because its smaller size keeps it suspended longer. PM2.5 is also more dangerous as it can bypass respiratory filters to enter the bloodstream.

questions.q: Q.29) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Many Himalayan glaciers with extensive natural debris cover are undergoing rapid thinning. Statement II: Debris layers reduce surface albedo and enhance heat absorption. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II is the correct explanation for Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II is the correct explanation for Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.e: While thick debris can insulate ice, most Himalayan glaciers have thin or patchy debris that reduces reflectivity (albedo) and absorbs solar heat. This absorbed heat is transferred to the ice, leading to faster melting and thinning.

questions.q: Q.30) Which of the following technologies can help reduce carbon emissions in the power sector? 1️⃣ Solar photovoltaic power 2️⃣ Concentrated solar power 3️⃣ Green hydrogen-based power 4️⃣ Offshore wind energy 5️⃣ Waste-to-energy incineration Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: I, II, III, IV and V
I, II, III and IV only
questions.e: Technologies 1-4 are clean or renewable sources that produce little to no CO2. However, waste-to-energy incineration releases CO2 from the combustion of plastics and fossil-based waste, so it is not a low-carbon power technology.

questions.q: Q.31) Freshwater sponges are considered useful bioindicators of aquatic pollution because:
o: they reproduce only in heavily polluted aquatic environments
they rapidly migrate away from polluted water bodies to cleaner habitats
they survive exclusively in unpolluted freshwater ecosystems
they filter large volumes of water and possess a high bioaccumulation ability for toxic heavy metals
questions.e: As multicellular filter feeders, freshwater sponges process large amounts of water and accumulate toxic metals like lead and arsenic in their bodies. This allows scientists to use them to measure the pollution levels of an ecosystem.

questions.q: Q.32) With reference to "marsupial" sometimes mentioned in the news, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Around two-thirds of them live in Australia. 2️⃣ They have one of the shortest gestation periods among all mammals. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: About two-thirds of the world's 330 marsupial species are found in Australia. They are unique for having extremely short pregnancies (12-40 days), after which the premature young continue developing in a pouch.

questions.q: Q.33) Jellyfish bloom, recently in news, is best described as:
o: a seasonal migration of jellyfish from deep oceans to coral reefs for breeding purposes
a rapid increase in jellyfish populations due to favourable environmental conditions
the permanent replacement of fish species by jellyfish in marine ecosystems
the artificial cultivation of jellyfish for commercial fisheries
questions.e: A jellyfish bloom is a sudden, massive increase in population triggered by factors like rising sea temperatures, overfishing of predators, and nutrient-rich runoff (eutrophication).

questions.q: Q.34) Consider the following statements: Statement I: The bar-headed goose is capable of flying at altitudes of 5,000 metres during migration. Statement II: The bar-headed goose has a higher concentration of red blood cells. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
questions.e: The bar-headed goose routinely crosses the Himalayas at altitudes above 5,000m. While it has physiological adaptations, it does not necessarily have more red blood cells; instead, its hemoglobin binds oxygen more strongly and its muscles use oxygen more efficiently.

questions.q: Q.35) Which of the following factors are essential for the functioning of Soil Microbial Fuel Cells (SMFCs)? 1️⃣ Anaerobic conditions around the anode region of the soil 2️⃣ Availability of biodegradable organic matter in the soil 3️⃣ Extremely high soil temperatures comparable to geothermal conditions 4️⃣ High-intensity artificial lighting to stimulate microbial metabolism Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: SMFCs generate electricity through soil microbes that break down organic matter. This process requires anaerobic conditions at the anode to ensure electron transfer and a steady supply of organic "fuel," but not extreme heat or artificial light.

questions.q: Q.36) Which one of the following most appropriately describes the term "net energy cliff"?
o: A sudden decline in total energy demand due to economic slowdown
A rapid shift from fossil fuels to renewable energy sources
A stage where the amount of energy required to extract, process, and deliver energy resources rapidly outgrows the net usable energy available to society
A situation where renewable energy fully replaces fossil fuels
questions.e: The net energy cliff occurs when the energy needed to produce energy (Energy Return on Investment or EROI) becomes so high that the actual usable energy left for society's economic growth begins to decline sharply.

questions.q: Q.37) The term "Relative decoupling" recently in news refers to:
o: complete segregation of economic growth from resource use
economic growth accompanied by a decline in absolute environmental degradation
economic growth with environmental damage increasing at slower rate
economic growth achieved without any increase in ecological footprint
questions.e: Decoupling refers to the link between the economy and environment. Relative decoupling means the economy grows faster than environmental damage, but damage still increases. Absolute decoupling would mean growth while damage actually decreases.

questions.q: Q.38) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Agroforestry systems located on higher slopes show higher carbon sequestration than those on lower slopes. Statement II: Lower slopes naturally accumulate more soil moisture and organic matter due to runoff from higher elevations. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
questions.e: Statement I is incorrect because trees on lower slopes actually grow better and sequester more carbon due to better moisture. Statement II is correct as lower slopes collect runoff, nutrients, and organic matter from above, facilitating healthier growth.

questions.q: Q.39) With reference to ecotones, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Their species richness and population density are often higher than the adjoining ecosystems. 2️⃣ Mangrove forests represent an ecotone between marine and terrestrial ecosystems. 3️⃣ Vertical ecotones are found in mountain ecosystems transitioning from forest to alpine tundra. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Ecotones are transitional zones that often exhibit the "edge effect," resulting in higher biodiversity. Mangroves (land-sea) and mountain transitions (forest-tundra) are classic examples of horizontal and vertical ecotones, respectively.

questions.q: Q.40) With reference to the Nitrogen Cycle, consider the following processes: 1️⃣ Ammonification 2️⃣ Nitrification 3️⃣ Nitrogen fixation Which of the above processes directly convert atmospheric nitrogen into biologically usable forms?
questions.e: Nitrogen fixation is the only process that takes inert N2 gas from the air and converts it into ammonia. Ammonification and Nitrification only transform nitrogen that is already present in organic matter or soil.

questions.q: Q.41) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Neuston: Attached microbial-algal community on submerged surfaces 2️⃣ Periphyton: Organisms living at the air-water interface 3️⃣ Nekton: Aquatic organisms that swim independent of currents 4️⃣ Benthos: Organisms living at the bottom of water bodies How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Nekton (active swimmers) and Benthos (bottom dwellers) are correctly matched. However, Neuston refers to organisms at the air-water interface, and Periphyton refers to the community attached to submerged surfaces.

questions.q: Q.42) Consider the following processes: 1️⃣ Rising sea level 2️⃣ Movement of sand and sandbars 3️⃣ Formation of narrow valleys by glaciers 4️⃣ Sinking of tectonic plate How many of the above can lead to the formation of estuaries?
questions.e: All four processes contribute to estuary formation: sea level rise creates coastal plain estuaries, sandbars create bar-built estuaries, glaciers create fjords, and tectonic sinking creates tectonic estuaries.

questions.q: Q.43) Consider the following statements with regard to mangroves: 1️⃣ They transfer the carbon to the soil, where it stays unaffected even if the tree is destroyed. 2️⃣ The Mangrove Alliance for Climate was launched during the 27th Conference of the Parties (COP27) of the UNFCCC. 3️⃣ They occupy nearly five per cent of India's total geographical area. 4️⃣ India's first mangrove park is being developed in Maharashtra. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Mangroves are efficient carbon sinks that store carbon in the soil. The MAC was launched at COP27. However, mangroves occupy only 0.15% (not 5%) of India's area. Maharashtra is developing India's first mangrove park at Gorai.

questions.q: Q.44) Consider the following activities: 1️⃣ Discharge of untreated sewage and effluents 2️⃣ Dumping of ballast water, fly ash and solid waste 3️⃣ Oil and gas exploration and mining 4️⃣ Traditional fishing and allied activities 5️⃣ Shipping and boat house operations How many of the above activities are restricted or regulated in CRZ-IV (water areas) as per the Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) rules in India?
questions.e: Under CRZ-IV, sewage discharge is prohibited, waste dumping is prohibited, and oil/gas mining is regulated. However, traditional fishing is permitted without restriction to protect local livelihoods, and navigation/shipping is generally allowed under standard maritime laws.

questions.q: Q.45) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Carbon Monoxide: Incomplete combustion in motor vehicles 2️⃣ Photochemical Smog: reaction involving NOx and VOCs 3️⃣ Silica: Vehicle exhausts and solvents 4️⃣ Black Carbon: Incomplete burning of biomass and diesel fuel 5️⃣ Hydrocarbons: Mining and stone quarrying activities How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2, and 4 are correct. Silica actually comes from crushing or blasting stone and concrete (not exhausts), while hydrocarbons typically arise from oil spills and industrial effluents (mining is associated with dust/silica).

questions.q: Q.46) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Phytoextraction: Accumulation of contaminants by plant roots and translocate them to upper parts 2️⃣ Phytostimulation: Biodegradation of contaminants by plant roots 3️⃣ Mycofiltration: Bioremediation of contaminants by algae How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Phytoextraction and Phytostimulation are correct descriptions. However, Mycofiltration uses fungal mycelium (mushrooms/fungi) for water treatment, not algae.

questions.q: Q.47) The concept "Colony Collapse Disorder" recently in news refers to:
o: a seasonal migration of entire bees colonies in response to abrupt climate shifts
a widespread fungal infection causing mass mortalities of bees inside the hive
a genetic mutation in queen bees leading to sterile worker populations and gradual colony extinction
a sudden disappearance of worker bees from a colony, while the queen and food reserves remain largely intact
questions.e: CCD is a phenomenon where the majority of worker bees disappear, leaving the queen and food behind. It is linked to multiple stressors including pesticides, habitat loss, and climate change.

questions.q: Q.48) Consider the following statements with regard to the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) in India: 1️⃣ Any project that could significantly alter land use or affect air, water, or ecosystems must obtain prior Environmental Clearance (EC). 2️⃣ All projects requiring the EC are appraised only at the Central level by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC). 3️⃣ Projects involving forest land require prior approval under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.e: EIA is mandatory for large-impact projects. However, projects are appraised at both Central (Category A) and State (Category B) levels. Statement III is correct as forest land diversion requires specific union government approval.

questions.q: Q.49) If a particular plant species is placed as Vulnerable under the IUCN's Red List of Threatened Species, what is the implication?
o: The species is close to qualifying for a threatened category in the near future.
The species survives only in captivity or cultivation.
The species is facing a very high risk of extinction in the near future.
The species is facing a high risk of extinction in the wild in the medium term.
questions.e: The "Vulnerable" category signifies a high risk of extinction in the medium term. "Near Threatened" applies to the near future, "Endangered" to a very high risk in the near future, and "Extinct in the Wild" to species surviving only in captivity.

questions.q: Q.50) Consider the following statements: Statement-I: India has reiterated that global mitigation pathways must reflect national circumstances and equity. Statement-II: The principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) requires all countries to adopt identical emission reduction targets. Statement-III: The principle of CBDR-RC allows flexibility in climate action based on historical responsibility and a country's capability. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
Only one of the Statements-II and III is correct and that explains Statement-I
questions.e: Statement II is false because CBDR-RC explicitly rejects identical targets, acknowledging different capabilities. Statement III is correct and provides the basis for Statement I's focus on national circumstances and equity.

questions.q: Q.51) Consider the following statements with regard to the Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022: 1️⃣ It prohibits any person from modifying or removing the identification mark of the specimen made by the Management authority. 2️⃣ It has inserted a new schedule for specimens listed for extinction under CITES. 3️⃣ It empowers the central government to declare areas adjacent to national parks and sanctuaries as a conservation reserve. How many of the statements given above are not correct?
questions.e: All three statements are correct under the 2022 Amendment. It protects CITES identification marks, adds a CITES schedule, and allows the central government to notify conservation reserves.

questions.q: Q.52) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Butanol and Acetone-Butanol-Ethanol (ABE) fuel mixtures are considered superior to ethanol. Statement II: Butanol has higher energy density, lower hygroscopicity, and better compatibility with existing internal combustion engines. Statement III: Glycerol is a common by-product formed during ethanol fermentation as well as during the transesterification process used in biodiesel production. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
questions.e: Both II and III are correct. However, only Statement II (regarding density and compatibility) explains why Butanol is superior to ethanol as a fuel. Statement III is an independent fact about by-products.

questions.q: Q.53) Which of the following species are endemic to India? 1️⃣ Nilgiri Tahr 2️⃣ Lion-tailed Macaque 3️⃣ Sangai Deer 4️⃣ Malabar civet 5️⃣ Red Panda Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: I, II, IV and V only
I, II, III and IV only
questions.e: Species 1-4 are found exclusively in India. The Red Panda is found in India but also lives in Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, and China, so it is not endemic to India.

questions.q: Q.54) In an ecosystem, the loss of which one of the following is most likely to cause structural collapse of the habitat, rather than immediate trophic imbalance?
questions.e: Foundation species (like corals or mangroves) physically create and maintain the habitat structure. Their loss causes the physical habitat to collapse, whereas apex predators primarily influence the food web (trophic levels).

questions.q: Q.55) Which of the following are advantages of Luminescent Solar Concentrators over Conventional Solar Panels? 1️⃣ Higher energy conversion efficiency 2️⃣ Require less photovoltaic material for electricity generation 3️⃣ Effective even under cloudy conditions 4️⃣ Reduced thermal losses and overheating effects 5️⃣ No emission losses during light concentration Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: I, II, III, IV and V
I, II, III and IV only
questions.e: LSCs use less PV material because they concentrate light onto small edge cells and are effective in diffuse light (clouds). However, they generally have lower overall efficiency than standard panels, and reabsorption/emission losses are a known limitation.

questions.q: Q.56) Photofermentation, dark fermentation, and biophotolysis are sometimes seen in the news in the context of:
questions.e: These biological processes utilize bacteria or algae to produce hydrogen. Photofermentation uses light and organic matter, while dark fermentation decomposes organic matter without light.

questions.q: Q.57) Recently at Ramsar CoP15, which one of the following countries introduced a resolution titled "Promoting Sustainable Lifestyles for the Wise Use of Wetlands"?
questions.e: At the July 2025 Ramsar CoP15 in Zimbabwe, India introduced this resolution to integrate lifestyle-based and behavioral approaches into global wetland conservation efforts.

questions.q: Q.58) With reference to the Bonn Climate Change Conference, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Along with the annual Conference of the Parties (COP), it is the only other regular climate summit hosted by the UNFCCC. 2️⃣ It primarily focuses on technical negotiations, and preparatory work for decisions to be taken at the COP. Which of the statements given above is/are not correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. The Bonn conference is the regular mid-year technical meeting that prepares draft decisions for the year-end COP. Since both are correct, the answer to "not correct" is "Neither I nor II."

questions.q: Q.59) The Government of India announced the preparation of a 'National Red List' as part of its global commitment towards biodiversity protection during which one of the following conferences/summits?
questions.e: India announced its National Red List roadmap during the 2025 IUCN World Conservation Congress in Abu Dhabi to assess the extinction risk of 11,000 native species.

questions.q: Q.60) With reference to India's first emission intensity targets for carbon-intensive sectors, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ These are built on the existing Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) energy efficiency framework. 2️⃣ The environmental compensation for non-compliance under this framework is proposed to be twice the average trading price of carbon credits. 3️⃣ The initial phase covers sectors such as aluminium, cement, and pulp and paper. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: India's new Greenhouse Gas Emission Intensity (GEI) framework builds on PAT and mandates environmental compensation of 2x the credit price for shortfalls. It initially targets high-emission sectors like cement and aluminium.

questions.q: Q.61) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Carbon dioxide accounts for more than 90% of all accumulated greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. 2️⃣ Methane is at least 25 times more potent than carbon dioxide in its heat-trapping capability. 3️⃣ Nitrous oxide has a shorter atmospheric lifetime than methane and contributes less to long-term global warming. Which of the statements given above is/are not correct?
questions.e: Statements I and II are correct. Statement III is incorrect because Nitrous oxide lives for 100-120 years (longer than methane's 12-14 years) and has a much higher global warming potential over a 100-year period.

questions.q: Q.62) With reference to the Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is not applicable to the forest areas of National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries and Tiger Reserves. 2️⃣ The Gram Sabha is the final authority in regulating transit permits for the transportation of minor forest produce. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The FRA specifically applies to all forest lands including National Parks and Protected Areas. The Gram Sabha is indeed the final authority for determining rights and regulating permits for minor forest produce.

questions.q: Q.63) Consider the following information: 1️⃣ Earthworm: Improves soil structure and nutrient cycling. 2️⃣ Fungi: Primary producer through photosynthesis. 3️⃣ Bacteria: Decomposition and nutrient recycling. In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched ?
questions.e: Rows 1 and 3 are correct. Fungi are heterotrophs (decomposers/symbionts) and cannot perform photosynthesis, so they are not primary producers.

questions.q: Q.64) With reference to Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They are notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 2️⃣ Coastal communities are permitted to undertake regulated livelihood activities in certain categories of MPAs. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: MPAs in India are notified under the 1972 Act. While some MPAs (like National Parks) have strict rules, others allow regulated traditional fishing or livelihood activities for local communities.

questions.q: Q.65) In the context of carbon offsetting projects, the term 'Additionality' refers to which one of the following?
o: Emission reductions that would not have occurred without carbon credit revenue
Emission reductions that are achieved at the lowest possible market cost
Emission reductions that are verified and certified by international agencies
Emission reductions that are permanently stored in natural ecosystems
questions.e: Additionality ensures that a project’s climate benefits are unique and only happened because of the extra funding from carbon credits, rather than being something required by existing laws or economic trends.

questions.q: Q.66) With reference to the Central Zoo Authority (CZA), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is a statutory body established under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. 2️⃣ Every zoo in India must obtain recognition from the Central Zoo Authority in order to operate legally. 3️⃣ It regulates the exchange and transfer of endangered animals listed under Schedule I and Schedule II of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. How many of the statements given above are not correct?
questions.e: All statements are correct. The CZA was established in 1992 as a statutory body to oversee all Indian zoos and manage the exchange of endangered species.

questions.q: Q.67) Which one of the following best describes the principle of "common heritage of mankind" under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)?
o: Resources of the deep seabed beyond national jurisdiction are owned collectively by humanity and managed for equitable benefit-sharing
Deep seabed resources beyond national jurisdiction belong to no State and can be freely appropriated by technologically advanced countries
Coastal States have exclusive sovereign rights to exploit all marine resources beyond their Exclusive Economic Zones
Marine resources are jointly controlled only by States bordering international waters
questions.e: This principle states that deep seabed resources in international waters (The Area) belong to humanity as a whole and must be managed for the benefit of all, particularly developing nations.

questions.q: Q.68) Which of the following are objectives of the National Afforestation Programme (NAP)? 1️⃣ It focuses on restoration of degraded forest lands. 2️⃣ It promotes community participation through Joint Forest Management Committees. 3️⃣ It aims to improve the livelihoods of forest-dependent communities. 4️⃣ It encourages monoculture plantations for export-oriented timber. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: NAP aims to restore degraded forests and support community livelihoods through JFMCs. It specifically encourages native multi-purpose species rather than monoculture or commercial timber plantations.

questions.q: Q.69) With reference to the Assessment Report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It provides a scientific basis for international climate negotiations. 2️⃣ It is prepared in a regular cycle of about five to seven years. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: IPCC reports synthesize global scientific knowledge to guide policy and negotiations like the UNFCCC. They are published in 5-7 year cycles to reflect the latest advances in science.

questions.q: Q.70) With reference to the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The waste generator is required to segregate bio-medical waste into colour-coded categories at the point of generation. 2️⃣ The Rules apply to all healthcare facilities, except blood banks. 3️⃣ The Rules mandate that treatment and disposal of bio-medical waste must take place within the district where it is generated. 4️⃣ The disposal of untreated bio-medical waste in municipal solid waste landfills is permitted under certain conditions. Which of the statements given above is/are not correct?
questions.e: Only statement I is correct. The rules DO apply to blood banks, they DO NOT restrict waste to one district (it can go to authorized facilities elsewhere), and they STRICTLY PROHIBIT untreated medical waste in municipal landfills.

questions.q: Q.71) Which of the following institutions are associated with the implementation of the Ramsar Convention? 1️⃣ International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) 2️⃣ Wetlands International 3️⃣ United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) 4️⃣ World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) 5️⃣ BirdLife International Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: I, II, IV and V only
I, II, III, IV and V
questions.e: The Ramsar Convention has officially recognized International Organization Partners (IOPs) including IUCN, Wetlands International, WWF, and BirdLife International. While the convention was adopted under UNESCO's auspices, UNESCO is not an operational partner today.

questions.q: Q.72) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Tropospheric ozone concentrations are increasing in many urban regions despite a decline in peak ozone episodes. Statement II: Rising atmospheric methane levels are offsetting the reduction in nitrogen dioxide emissions. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
questions.e: While urban centers have reduced local NOx emissions (cutting peak ozone), global methane levels are rising. Methane acts as an ozone precursor, increasing the baseline tropospheric ozone levels even as peak episodes fall.

questions.q: Q.73) Consider the following information: 1️⃣ Cold Desert: Himachal Pradesh - Included in UNESCO'S World Network of Biosphere Reserves. 2️⃣ Gulf of Mannar: Tamil Nadu - India's first marine biosphere reserve. 3️⃣ Dihang-Dibang: Assam - Lies entirely within the Eastern Himalaya biodiversity hotspot. In how many of the above rows is the information correctly matched?
questions.e: Rows 1 and 2 are correct. Row 3 is incorrect because the Dihang-Dibang Biosphere Reserve is located in Arunachal Pradesh, not Assam.

questions.q: Q.74) In which of the following cases is prior environmental clearance mandatory under India's Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) framework? 1️⃣ Expansion of national highways within city limits 2️⃣ Mining of minor minerals below threshold limits 3️⃣ Offshore and onshore oil and gas exploration 4️⃣ Establishment of Soda ash industry 5️⃣ Expansion of metallurgical industries Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: I, II, III and V only
questions.e: Projects 3, 4, and 5 are high-impact activities listed in the EIA schedule. Highway expansions within city limits (without new alignment) and mining below certain thresholds are generally exempt from the prior EC requirement.

questions.q: Q.75) Consider the following statements with regard to the Indian Pangolin: 1️⃣ It is a nocturnal, insectivorous mammal. 2️⃣ It is the only scaly mammal found in India. 3️⃣ It is listed in Schedule II of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. 4️⃣ It is listed in CITES Appendix I, prohibiting its international commercial trade. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2, and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because both Indian and Chinese pangolins are listed in Schedule I (highest protection) of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, not Schedule II.

questions.q: Q.76) Consider the following statements with regard to National Board for Wildlife (NBWL): 1️⃣ It makes recommendations on the setting and managing of National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries. 2️⃣ It has the Chief of Army Staff and Defence Secretary as its members. 3️⃣ Its Standing Committee deals with project-level clearances and policy decisions related to wildlife conservation. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The NBWL is a statutory body that advises on protected areas and includes defense officials as members. However, statement III is slightly inaccurate as the Board handles broad policy, while the Standing Committee primarily focuses on specific project clearances.

questions.q: Q.77) Consider the following statements with regard to microplastics: 1️⃣ Some microplastics originate from synthetic textiles. 2️⃣ Some microplastics act as vectors for pollutants. 3️⃣ Some plastics are manufactured in microscopic sizes. 4️⃣ Some microplastics carry microbes or pathogens. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All statements are correct. Microplastics come from textile fibers, can absorb toxic chemicals (acting as vectors), are sometimes made small intentionally (microbeads), and can carry antibiotic-resistant pathogens.

questions.q: Q.78) Consider the following areas: 1️⃣ Public health 2️⃣ Education 3️⃣ Affordable housing 4️⃣ Resilience to disasters 5️⃣ Use of local materials How many of the above does the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 11 directly focus on?
questions.e: SDG 11 focuses on making cities sustainable. It directly targets affordable housing (11.1), disaster resilience (11.B), and building with local materials (11.C). Public health and education are the focuses of SDG 3 and SDG 4, respectively.

questions.q: Q.79) With reference to Indian fauna, the Great Indian Bustard, Bengal Florican and Lesser Florican are classified as:
questions.e: These bustard species are flagship indicators of the health of arid and semi-arid grassland ecosystems in India.

questions.q: Q.80) With reference to the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) Champions of the Earth Award, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is the United Nations' highest environmental honour. 2️⃣ It is only awarded to environmental activists who mobilise public action and behavioural change through example and advocacy. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: It is indeed the highest UN environmental honor. However, it is not just for activists; it has four categories including Policy Leadership, Entrepreneurial Vision, and Science/Innovation.

questions.q: Q.81) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ India ranks first globally in the production of rice bran oil, castor seed, safflower and niger. 2️⃣ Oilseeds hold the second-highest acreage and production value in Indian agriculture after food grains. 3️⃣ Andhra Pradesh and Telangana are major oil palm growing States and account for 98% of total production. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India leads globally in several minor oilseeds and rice bran oil. Oilseeds are second only to food grains in acreage. Andhra and Telangana dominate the oil palm sector, producing 98% of the national output.

questions.q: Q.82) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Neem coated urea has reduced nitrogen use inefficiency in Indian agriculture. Statement II: Neem coating increases nitrogen availability by improving water retention capacity of soils. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above Statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II is the correct explanation for Statement I
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II is not the correct explanation for Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
questions.e: Neem coating improves efficiency by acting as a natural nitrification inhibitor, slowing down the conversion of nitrogen so plants can absorb it better. Statement II is incorrect as it does not significantly alter the soil's water retention capacity.

questions.q: Q.83) The increasing use of agricultural drones in India is directly associated with which of the following outcomes? 1️⃣ Reduction in excessive use of pesticides and agrochemicals 2️⃣ Generation of geospatial data useful for precision farming 3️⃣ Early identification of pest infestation 4️⃣ Reduction in labour dependency Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Agricultural drones enable precision spraying (reducing chemical use), capture spectral data for mapping, monitor crop health for pests, and automate hazardous manual tasks like pesticide application.

questions.q: Q.84) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Pulses fix atmospheric nitrogen through symbiotic Rhizobium bacteria. 2️⃣ Pulses are mainly grown under rainfed conditions in India. 3️⃣ India is the world's largest producer and consumer of pulses in the world. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Pulses enrich soil fertility via nitrogen fixation and are primarily a rainfed crop in India (80-87%). India is the global leader in both producing and consuming pulses.

questions.q: Q.85) Which one of the following crops is most vulnerable to groundwater depletion when cultivated extensively under assured irrigation systems?
questions.e: Rice is extremely water-intensive, requiring standing water. In areas like Punjab and Haryana, extensive rice cultivation under irrigation has been directly linked to the rapid depletion of groundwater.

questions.q: Q.86) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Zero Budget Natural Farming leads to improved fruit size and vegetative growth in crops. Statement II: Zero Budget Natural Farming practices supply synthetic nitrogen and phosphorus fertilisers at critical growth stages. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above Statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II is the correct explanation for Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II is the correct explanation for Statement I
questions.e: ZBNF has been shown to improve fruit quality and plant vigor through better soil health. However, a core principle of ZBNF is the total avoidance of all synthetic fertilizers.

questions.q: Q.87) Consider the following functions: 1️⃣ Promoting integrated development of coconut cultivation and industry 2️⃣ Fixing minimum support price for coconuts 3️⃣ Fixing grades, specifications and standards for coconut and its products Which of the above is/are functions of the Coconut Development Board?
questions.e: The Board handles industry development and standard-setting. However, the MSP for copra/coconut is recommended by the CACP, not the Coconut Development Board.

questions.q: Q.88) Consider the following information: 1️⃣ Rice: Eastern India - Clayey alluvial soil with high humidity and temperature. 2️⃣ Sugarcane: Tropical as well as sub-tropical regions of India - A long frost-free period with adequate sunlight and moisture. 3️⃣ Jute: Lower Gangetic Plain of India - Grey alluvial soil with high rainfall. In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
questions.e: All rows are correct. Rice thrives in humid Eastern India, Sugarcane requires frost-free periods across India, and Jute is concentrated in the high-rainfall Gangetic plains.

questions.q: Q.89) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Potato 2️⃣ Chilli 3️⃣ Turmeric 4️⃣ Tomato 5️⃣ Timru How many of the crops given above are not native to India?
questions.e: Potato, Chilli, and Tomato were all introduced to India by Portuguese traders. Turmeric and Timru are native to the Indian sub-continent/South Asia.

questions.q: Q.90) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Onion 2️⃣ Fertilisers 3️⃣ Drugs 4️⃣ Petroleum products 5️⃣ Potatoes How many of the above fall under the Essential Commodities Act of 1955?
questions.e: Currently, fertilisers, drugs, and petroleum products are on the essential list. Onions and potatoes (along with cereals and pulses) were removed from the list via a Bill in 2020.

questions.q: Q.91) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Growing more than one crop simultaneously on the same field can reduce inter-annual yield variability under uncertain climatic conditions. 2️⃣ Cultivation of a single crop repeatedly on the same field facilitates better pest and disease resistance due to uniform crop management practices. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Intercropping (Statement I) spreads risk and reduces yield variability. Statement II is incorrect because monoculture (single crop) actually increases pest pressure by providing a continuous host and food source for specific pathogens.

questions.q: Q.92) Consider the following crops: 1️⃣ Wheat 2️⃣ Barley 3️⃣ Mustard 4️⃣ Rice 5️⃣ Red gram (Tur) How many of the above are typically grown during the rabi season in India under cool temperature conditions?
questions.e: Wheat, Barley, and Mustard are classic rabi crops that need cool winters. Rice and Red gram (Tur) are kharif crops that require the warmth and high rainfall of the monsoon season.

questions.q: Q.93) Which of the following groups consists entirely of crops covered under the Minimum Support Price (MSP) system in India?
questions.e: Group B is correct. Group A is wrong because Sugarcane has FRP (not MSP). Group C is wrong because Onion has no MSP. Group D is wrong because Tea is a plantation crop with no MSP.

questions.q: Q.94) Which of the following are the objectives of the "Mission for Cotton Productivity"? 1️⃣ Focusing on the three pillars of Certification, Traceability, and Branding 2️⃣ Developing high-yielding varieties like Extra Long Staple (ELS) cotton 3️⃣ Providing farmers with cutting-edge scientific and technological support 4️⃣ Developing climate-smart, pest-resistant varieties Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Mission focuses on high-yield ELS cotton, tech support, and climate-smart varieties. Pillar 1 (Branding/Traceability) is specifically an objective of the separate 'Kasturi Cotton Bharat' program.

questions.q: Q.95) With reference to India's position in global agricultural production and trade, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ India is the largest producer of makhana (fox nut) in the world. 2️⃣ India is the largest exporter of rice in the world in terms of quantity. 3️⃣ India is the largest producer as well as the largest exporter of cereal products in the world. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: India holds an 80% global share in makhana and is its top exporter. India is also the world's largest exporter of rice and, according to FAO 2023, the top producer and exporter of cereal products globally.

questions.q: Q.96) Consider the following agricultural practices: 1️⃣ Stubble retention 2️⃣ Zero tillage 3️⃣ Intercropping 4️⃣ Green manuring 5️⃣ Mulching How many of the above help in conserving soil moisture under rainfed agriculture?
questions.e: All these practices improve soil structure and organic matter, which directly enhances the water-holding capacity and moisture retention of the soil.

questions.q: Q.97) With reference to the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is a member of the United Nations Development Group. 2️⃣ It is dedicated to eradicating poverty and hunger in rural areas of developing countries. 3️⃣ India is a founding member of IFAD. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: IFAD is a specialized UN agency and UNDG member. Its mandate is rural poverty eradication, and India is indeed one of its founding members.

questions.q: Q.98) Consider the following statements regarding India's agriculture sector: Statement I: Agriculture contributes merely 18 per cent to India's GDP. Statement II: Agriculture in India is characterised by low labour productivity. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement-I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: Agriculture uses 46% of India's workforce but only produces 18% of the GDP. This disconnect is a direct result of low per-worker productivity in the sector.

questions.q: Q.99) Which of the following best describes the 'Paira' cropping system?
o: Growing two crops simultaneously on the same land with equal duration
Raising crops using irrigation without relying on rainfall
Cultivating the next crop only after complete harvest and conventional tillage
Sowing short-duration pulse or oilseed crops into standing paddy fields before harvest
questions.e: Paira (or Utera) is a conservation practice in Eastern India where pulses or oilseeds are sown in standing rice fields before harvest to utilize the existing soil moisture.

questions.q: Q.100) With reference to the Global Seed Vault, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is a facility that stores the world's largest collection of crop seeds. 2️⃣ It is located on the Alexander Island of Antarctica. 3️⃣ It is jointly owned by the G7 member countries. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault is the largest repository of its kind. However, it is located in the Arctic (Svalbard, Norway), not Antarctica, and it is owned by Norway, not the G7.

questions.q: Q.1) Consider the following statements with regard to the Constitution of India: 1️⃣ Article 25 protects religious faith and not religious practices which may run counter to public order, health or morality. 2️⃣ Article 23 allows the State to impose compulsory service for public purposes on anyone with no obligation to pay for it. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Article 25 guarantees the freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion, but this right is subject to public order, morality, and health. Article 23 prohibits forced labor but allows the State to impose compulsory service for public purposes without discrimination.

questions.q: Q.2) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ No law can be enacted if it is contrary to Fundamental Rights guaranteed under the Constitution—Part III 2️⃣ Provision for early childhood care and education to children below the age of six years—Part IV 3️⃣ Promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India—Preamble 4️⃣ Provide primary education in the mother tongue for children from linguistic minority groups—Part IV-A. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pair 1 is correct as Article 13 (Part III) ensures laws contrary to Fundamental Rights are void. Pair 2 is correct as Article 45 (Part IV) provides for early childhood care. Pair 3 is incorrect as this is a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A, and Pair 4 is incorrect as Article 350A is in Part XVII.

questions.q: Q.3) With reference to Indian polity, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Every Minister and the Attorney-General has a right to speak and take part in the proceedings of either House of parliament, but not in a joint sitting. 2️⃣ A joint sitting cannot be held if Lok Sabha is dissolved, even if it has been convened already before the dissolution of Lok Sabha. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect because Article 88 grants Ministers and the Attorney-General the right to speak in joint sittings. Statement 2 is incorrect because under Article 108, if the President has notified the intention to summon a joint sitting, it can be held even if the Lok Sabha is subsequently dissolved.

questions.q: Q.4) Consider the following statements: Statement I: When the annual Union Budget is not passed by the Lok Sabha, the Prime Minister submits the resignation of the Council of Ministers. Statement II: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, and losing approval of the Budget indicates that the government has lost the confidence of the House. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
questions.e: In the Indian parliamentary system, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. Failure to pass the Budget is viewed as a loss of confidence, requiring the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers to resign.

questions.q: Q.5) "To protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures" is a provision made under the:
questions.e: This provision is a Fundamental Duty of every citizen of India as per Article 51A(g) of the Constitution, which was added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

questions.q: Q.6) Consider the following statements with reference to the Advisory Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court: 1️⃣ The President cannot seek advice on questions regarding the validity of a statute already in force or a constitutional provision. 2️⃣ The Supreme Court can refuse to tender its opinion to the President in case of any pre-constitutional treaty. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect because the President can seek advice on questions of law or fact, including the validity of existing statutes. Statement 2 is incorrect because while the Court may refuse advice under Article 143, it must tender its opinion on pre-constitutional treaties under Article 143.

questions.q: Q.7) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ A Bill pending for the assent of the Governor will lapse if the State Assembly dissolves. 2️⃣ If a Bill is sent to the State Legislature for reconsideration and if it is passed again by the State Legislature, then the Governor should mandatorily give his assent. 3️⃣ When the Governor reserves a bill for the consideration of the President, the Governor's role ceases for that Bill. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect because a bill pending for assent does not lapse on dissolution. Statement 2 is correct as the Governor must assent if a bill is passed again after reconsideration. Statement 3 is correct as the Governor's role ends once a bill is reserved for the President.

questions.q: Q.8) With reference to Indian polity, which of the following statements are correct? 1️⃣ Vice-President is elected by an Electoral College, which consists of the members of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, including nominated members. 2️⃣ The Election Commission of India, in consultation with the President, appoints a Returning Officer for the election of Vice President of India. 3️⃣ In India, the President is regarded as a constituent part of the Parliament. 4️⃣ The Constitution provides that when vacancies occur in the offices of both the President and the Vice-President, the Chief Justice of India will discharge the functions of the President. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 2 is incorrect as the ECI consults the Central Government, not the President, for appointing the Returning Officer. Statement 4 is incorrect because the Chief Justice's role in this contingency is provided by a statutory law (Act of 1969), not the Constitution itself.

questions.q: Q.9) With reference to the Lok Adalats, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Under the Legal Services Authority Act, 1987, the State legislature has the requisite powers to specify procedure for the determination of any dispute coming before Lok Adalats. 2️⃣ It is mandatory for the Centre and every State Authority to establish permanent Lok Adalats in respect of public utility services. 3️⃣ Lok Adalats have no jurisdiction over an offence, which is not compoundable under any law. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Lok Adalat itself has the power to specify its own procedure under Section 22. Statements 2 and 3 are correct regarding the mandatory establishment of permanent Lok Adalats for public utilities and their lack of jurisdiction over non-compoundable offenses.

questions.q: Q.10) Consider the following organizations/bodies in India: 1️⃣ Central Bureau of Investigation 2️⃣ National Commission for Safai Karamcharis 3️⃣ National Human Rights Commission 4️⃣ Rehabilitation Council of India 5️⃣ National Security Council 6️⃣ National Commission for Women. How many of the above are statutory bodies?
questions.e: Only the NHRC, Rehabilitation Council of India, and National Commission for Women are statutory. The CBI was established by resolution, the NSC by executive order, and the NCSK currently functions as a non-statutory body.

questions.q: Q.11) Consider the following statements with regard to the Neolithic period in India: 1️⃣ The development of agriculture resulted in surplus food production, which enabled the emergence of large, settled villages and permanent structures. 2️⃣ The earliest archaeological evidence of plant and animal domestication in the Indian subcontinent is associated with Neolithic sites located in southern India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct as agriculture led to permanent settlements. Statement 2 is incorrect because the earliest evidence is found in north-western India, specifically at sites like Mehrgarh in present-day Pakistan.

questions.q: Q.12) In the context of Indus Valley Civilisation, consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Mohenjodaro—Pashupati seal 2️⃣ Lothal—Walled citadel 3️⃣ Surkotada—Pot burials 4️⃣ Banawali—Highly systematic drainage. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pair 1 is correct. Pair 2 is incorrect because Lothal's citadel was not separately walled. Pair 3 is correct. Pair 4 is incorrect because Banawali is noted for a lack of systematic drainage.

questions.q: Q.13) In the early vedic period, Vrajapati was:
o: administrative head of a settled village unit
permanent commander of the tribal standing army
chief of a pastoral clan responsible for ritual and social leadership
officer who was in charge of pasture lands
questions.e: In the Rig Vedic period, the Vrajapati was the official in charge of pasture lands. Other officials included the Senani (commander) and Gramani (head of the village).

questions.q: Q.14) Consider the following information: 1️⃣ Satyameva Jayate—Truth alone triumphs—Mundaka Upanishad 2️⃣ Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam—Assimilation of all societies into single culture—Maha Upanishad 3️⃣ Ahimsa Paramo Dharma—Non-violence is the highest duty—Chandogya Upanishad. In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
questions.e: Row 1 is correctly matched. Row 2 is incorrect because the meaning is "the whole world is one family." Row 3 is incorrect because "Ahimsa Paramo Dharma" is associated with the Mahabharata, not the Chandogya Upanishad.

questions.q: Q.15) Arrange the following metals in the correct chronological order of their beginning of use in ancient India, from the earliest to the latest: 1️⃣ Iron 2️⃣ Copper 3️⃣ Bronze. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Copper was the first metal used (Chalcolithic), followed by Bronze (Indus Valley Civilization), and finally Iron (Iron Age/Later Vedic period).

questions.q: Q.16) Consider the following statements with regard to the Ajivika Sect: 1️⃣ It was popular in Magadha region and founded by Makkhali Gosala. 2️⃣ The followers of this sect held that the affairs of the entire universe were ordered by a cosmic force called niyati. 3️⃣ Ajivikas practised austerities rather than pursue any purposeful goal. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: All statements are correct. The sect was founded by Makkhali Gosala, believed in the absolute rule of destiny (niyati), and practiced severe austerities because they believed human effort could not change fate.

questions.q: Q.17) With reference to the core philosophical concepts of Buddhism, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Anicca refers to the impermanent nature of all conditioned phenomena. 2️⃣ Anatta denotes the absence of a permanent, unchanging self or soul. 3️⃣ Dukkha signifies suffering or unsatisfactoriness inherent in worldly existence. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are the fundamental "Three Marks of Existence" in Buddhism. Anicca (impermanence), Anatta (non-self), and Dukkha (suffering) are core tenets of Buddhist philosophy.

questions.q: Q.18) "The world is made of soul (jiva) and matter (ajiva), which are eternal. The coming together of jiva and ajiva create karma (action), which leads to an endless cycle of birth and rebirth. To free oneself from karma, one has to practice severe austerities and self-mortification". The above concept of life is preached by:
questions.e: This dualistic philosophy of Jiva and Ajiva, the accumulation of karma through their interaction, and the path to liberation through severe austerities are central to Jainism.

questions.q: Q.19) Which of the following places is not associated with Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts?
questions.e: Kalsi, Sannati, and Girnar are sites of Major Rock Edicts. Shishupalgarh is an ancient fortified city but does not host Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts; nearby edicts are at Dhauli.

questions.q: Q.20) With reference to to the Sangam and post-Sangam Tamil literature, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Tolkappiyam is the earliest extant Tamil grammatical work and deals with poetry as well as the society and culture of its time. 2️⃣ The Pathinen Kilkanakku belong to the post-Sangam period and reflect a social and cultural set-up different from the Sangam age. Which of the above statements is/are not correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. Tolkappiyam is the oldest Tamil grammar and provides cultural context. The Pathinen Kilkanakku (Eighteen Lower Texts) belong to the post-Sangam period.

questions.q: Q.21) With reference to eclipses, consider the following statements: Statement I: A total solar eclipse is the result of the apparent angular size of the Moon. Statement II: The Moon orbits Earth in an elliptical path. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.e: The Moon's elliptical orbit changes its distance from Earth, thus changing its apparent angular size. When it is large enough to cover the Sun's disc, a total solar eclipse occurs.

questions.q: Q.22) With reference to volcanic eruptions, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ At convergent boundaries, subduction generates silica-rich viscous magma, leading to highly explosive volcanic eruptions. 2️⃣ Shield volcanoes erupt low-viscosity basaltic magma that spreads over vast areas. 3️⃣ Submarine volcanic eruptions do not contribute to the formation of new landmasses. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect as submarine volcanoes frequently create new landmasses and islands, such as Surtsey or Nishinoshima.

questions.q: Q.23) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Landscapes progress through all stages of youth, maturity, and old age under conditions of long-term tectonic stability. Statement II: Continuous tectonic uplift accelerates the cycle of erosion and enables the landscape to reach the peneplain stage more quickly. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
