Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
questions.e: Statement I is correct based on the Davisian cycle. Statement II is incorrect because continuous uplift disrupts the cycle and prevents the formation of a peneplain.

questions.q: Q.24) A particular City in India has the following characteristics: 1️⃣ It is located on the Tropic of Cancer. 2️⃣ It was considered the "Greenwich of India" by ancient Indian astronomers. 3️⃣ It is situated on the bank of the river that travels from South to North. Which one among the following cities has all the above characteristics?
questions.e: Ujjain is on the Tropic of Cancer, was the Prime Meridian for ancient Indian geographers, and is on the bank of the Kshipra river, which flows from South to North.

questions.q: Q.25) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Auroras occur predominantly in high-latitude regions. Statement II: Earth's magnetic field lines converge near the poles. Statement III: High-energy charged particles from the solar wind collide with atmospheric gases. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
questions.e: Auroras occur at high latitudes because Earth's magnetic field directs solar wind particles to converge at the poles (Statement II), where they collide with atmospheric gases to produce light (Statement III).

questions.q: Q.26) With reference to Typhoons, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is a non-frontal spatially large low-pressure system with organized convection. 2️⃣ It typically forms where sea surface temperatures exceed 26°C. 3️⃣ Ocean warming leads to frequent and rapid intensification of typhoons. 4️⃣ All typhoons rotate clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere due to the Coriolis effect. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 4 is incorrect because typhoons in the Northern Hemisphere rotate counter-clockwise. Statements 1, 2, and 3 correctly describe the nature, formation conditions, and intensification of typhoons.

questions.q: Q.27) With reference to the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is characterized by sea surface temperature differences between the Pacific Ocean and the Indian Ocean. 2️⃣ A positive IOD event strengthens the monsoon winds moving towards the Indian subcontinent. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect because IOD involves temperature differences between the western and eastern Indian Ocean. Statement 2 is correct as a positive IOD enhances the Indian monsoon.

questions.q: Q.28) Which of the following statements are correct with regard to the Brahmani River? 1️⃣ It is formed by the confluence of the Sankh and South Koel rivers. 2️⃣ The Brahmani delta is the site of the Bhitarkanika Wildlife Sanctuary. 3️⃣ The principal tributaries of this river are Sankh, Tikra, and Karo. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Brahmani is formed by the Sankh and South Koel, supports the Bhitarkanika ecosystem, and has the Sankh, Tikra, and Karo as major tributaries.

questions.q: Q.29) Consider the following statements with regard to Great Nicobar Island: 1️⃣ It is the northernmost island of the Nicobar Archipelago. 2️⃣ The Shompen tribes live in the forests of the Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve. 3️⃣ Saddle Peak, the highest elevation of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, is located on this island. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect as Great Nicobar is the southernmost island. Statement 3 is incorrect as Saddle Peak is in North Andaman. Statement 2 is correct regarding the Shompen tribe.

questions.q: Q.30) Consider the following statements: Statement I: The Eastern Himalayan Syntaxis (EHS) marks a zone where the northward-moving Indian Plate continues to collide with and underthrust the Eurasian Plate. Statement II: The convergence rate of continental plates is faster in the Eastern Himalayas than the average across the Himalayas. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: Statement I is correct about the EHS. Statement II is incorrect because the average convergence rate is broadly similar across the entire Himalayan arc; the intensity at EHS is due to structural complexity.

questions.q: Q.31) Consider the following ecological adaptations seen in plants: 1️⃣ Releasing volatile organic chemicals 2️⃣ Leaves modified into spines 3️⃣ Pneumatophores in roots 4️⃣ Needle like leaves 5️⃣ Use of camouflage method. How many of the above are used by plants to protect themselves from herbivores?
questions.e: VOCs, spines, needle-like leaves, and camouflage are defenses against herbivores. Pneumatophores (breathing roots) are adaptations for respiration in oxygen-deficient marshy soils, not a defense against herbivory.

questions.q: Q.32) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Dampa Tiger Reserve—Manipur 2️⃣ Papikonda National Park—Andhra Pradesh 3️⃣ Sri Venkateswara Wildlife Sanctuary—Karnataka 4️⃣ Raimona National Park—Assam. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pair 1 is incorrect (Mizoram). Pair 2 is correct. Pair 3 is incorrect (Andhra Pradesh). Pair 4 is correct.

questions.q: Q.33) Consider the following statements with regard to the Integrated Biodiversity Assessment Tool (IBAT) Alliance: 1️⃣ It is a global partnership consisting of BirdLife International, Conservation International, IUCN, and UNEP-WCMC. 2️⃣ It provides trusted data to assess biodiversity risks and align with global frameworks to support nature-positive goals. 3️⃣ It works under the secretariat of the United Nations Environment Programme. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect as IBAT is an independent multi-institutional partnership, not a secretariat under UNEP.

questions.q: Q.34) Regarding Gharial (Gavialis gangeticus), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They are not covered under the Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats Scheme for Protection of Wildlife. 2️⃣ It is the only known crocodilian species that shares its habitat with the Saltwater Crocodile in the Sundarbans. 3️⃣ It is the only crocodilian which shows a visible sexual dimorphism. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect as Gharials are a priority species under the IDWH scheme. Statement 2 is incorrect as Gharials are freshwater species and do not inhabit the saline Sundarbans. Statement 3 is correct (the 'ghara' on the male's snout).

questions.q: Q.35) With reference to the classification of industries by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Industries are classified by CPCB based on Pollution Index, a matrix which was introduced in 2016. 2️⃣ Common Effluent Treatment Plants and Sewage Treatment Plants are classified under the 'Green' category. 3️⃣ Blue Category industries are involved in management of environmental pollution arising from domestic activities. 4️⃣ Industries classified under the 'White' category are exempted from the requirement of obtaining both 'Consent to Establish' and 'Consent to Operate'. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 2 is incorrect as CETPs and STPs are in the 'Blue' category. Statements 1, 3, and 4 correctly describe the PI matrix, Blue category purpose, and White category exemptions.

questions.q: Q.36) With reference to Trichloroethylene and Perchloroethylene, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They are primarily used as solvents in the dry-cleaning industry and as degreasing agents for metal parts. 2️⃣ Long-term exposure to these chemicals is permissible as they are biodegradable and non-carcinogenic. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect as these are Persistent Organic Pollutants, resist natural degradation, and are linked to cancer and organ damage.

questions.q: Q.37) Consider the following Green Houses Gases: 1️⃣ Chloroform 2️⃣ Methane 3️⃣ Nitrous oxide 4️⃣ Carbon tetrachloride 5️⃣ Hydrofluorocarbons. Which one of the following gives the correct arrangement of above gases as per their Global Warming Potential Value?
questions.e: Global Warming Potential (100-year) order is HFCs (potency up to 14,800), Carbon tetrachloride (1,730), Nitrous oxide , Methane (27-30), and Chloroform (31 but very short-lived).

questions.q: Q.38) With reference to the National Bio Energy Programme, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is being implemented by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. 2️⃣ It aims to promote Biomass Briquettes and Pellets manufacturing plants to support co-firing in thermal power plants. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect as it is implemented by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE). Statement 2 is correct as a sub-scheme specifically supports briquette and pellet manufacturing.

questions.q: Q.39) With reference to the Pradhan Mantri Jaiv Indhan Vatavaran Anukool Fasal Awashesh Nivaran (PM-JI-VAN) Scheme, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1️⃣ It is implemented by the Centre for High Technology, under the administrative control of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. 2️⃣ It focuses on providing financial support for setting up Second Generation bio-ethanol projects using lignocellulosic biomass and other renewable feedstocks. 3️⃣ It aims to establish Compressed Biogas plants across the country to reduce import dependency on Natural Gas. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect as the establishment of Compressed Biogas plants is the mandate of the SATAT initiative, not PM-JI-VAN.

questions.q: Q.40) The 'Production Gap Report', recently seen in the news, quantifies which of the following discrepancies?
o: The disparity between the installed renewable energy capacity and the capacity required to phase out coal-fired power plants by 2030.
The difference between governments planned fossil fuel production and the global production levels consistent with the Paris Agreement limits.
The gap between the climate finance promised by developed nations and the actual funds mobilized for the Global South.
The difference between the projected global greenhouse gas emissions and the emission levels required to limit warming to 1.5°C.
questions.e: The Production Gap Report tracks the discrepancy between government-planned fossil fuel production and levels consistent with the 1.5°C or 2°C warming limits.

questions.q: Q.41) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Quantum bits (qubits) can exist in superposition states and represent multiple values simultaneously. 2️⃣ Quantum key distribution enables secure communication by detecting any interference during key exchange. 3️⃣ Quantum tunneling allows particles to penetrate energy barriers due to their wave-like nature. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All statements are correct. Qubits use superposition, QKD detects eavesdropping via disturbances, and tunneling is a quantum wave-particle phenomenon.

questions.q: Q.42) Consider the following technologies: 1️⃣ Solid-State Batteries 2️⃣ Hydrogen Internal Combustion Engines 3️⃣ Plug-in Hybrid Electric Systems. How many of the above are classified under low-emission vehicle technologies?
questions.e: All three are considered low-emission technologies. Solid-state batteries support EVs, H2-ICE burning hydrogen is cleaner than fossil fuels, and PHEVs significantly reduce emissions compared to conventional ICEs.

questions.q: Q.43) Consider the following pairs with regards to Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs): 1️⃣ Fixed-wing UAV—Aerial mapping and large-scale surveying 2️⃣ VTOL / Hybrid-VTOL UAV—Medical supplies to disaster-stricken areas 3️⃣ Tactical UAV—Spraying of fertilizer in agricultural fields. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Pair 3 is incorrect as Tactical UAVs are for military reconnaissance and intelligence, while agricultural spraying is done by commercial/agricultural UAVs.

questions.q: Q.44) With reference to the sodium-ion (Na-ion) battery, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It uses nanotechnology to significantly lower charge time and increase charge cycles. 2️⃣ It is safer to use as it has a higher operating temperature range. 3️⃣ It is less energy dense and has less storage capacity compared to lithium-based batteries. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All statements are correct. Recent Indian innovations have improved Na-ion charging/cycling, and they are safer and more abundant than lithium, though less energy-dense.

questions.q: Q.45) The HMX and TNT, sometimes seen in the news, are:
questions.e: HMX (High Melting Explosive) and TNT (Trinitrotoluene) are organic compounds used as military-grade high explosives in warheads and demolition.

questions.q: Q.46) Which of the following activities constitute a service sector in the economy? 1️⃣ Insurance and Banking 2️⃣ Consultancy 3️⃣ Transportation and Logistics 4️⃣ Repairs of Machine. Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
questions.e: All these activities belong to the tertiary (service) sector. This includes finance, transportation, and maintenance services like machine repair.

questions.q: Q.47) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Veblen goods experience an increase in demand as their prices rise. 2️⃣ Essential goods show negligible price elasticity in case of their price rise. 3️⃣ Increased demand for a good decreases the demand of its complementary good. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because complementary goods are used together; increased demand for one increases demand for the other (e.g., cars and petrol).

questions.q: Q.48) Suppose the Balance of Payments data of a country in a given financial year shows the export of merchandise worth 45,000 crores and the import of merchandise worth 65,000 crores. The economy also records an export of services (software and tourism) valued at ₹30,000 crores and an import of services worth 12,000 crores. Additionally, net private transfers from workers abroad are 10,000 crores, while net investment income paid to foreigners stands at ₹5,000 crores. Which of the following statements are correct? 1️⃣ The Merchandise Trade Deficit for the year is 20,000 crores. 2️⃣ The overall Trade Balance is in surplus by 10,000 crores. 3️⃣ The Balance on Invisibles shows a surplus of 23,000 crores. 4️⃣ The Current Account Balance shows a final surplus of ₹3,000 crores. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct (45k-65k = -20k). Statement 3 is correct (18k net services + 10k transfers - 5k income = 23k). Statement 4 is correct (-20k + 23k = +3k). Statement 2 is incorrect as the overall trade balance is a deficit of 2,000 crores.

questions.q: Q.49) Consider the following statements: Statement I: In the budget 2025-26, the Union government allocated more than 3% of GDP towards capital expenditure. Statement II: Capital expenditure has a higher multiplier effect on the economy's output and employment generation. Which of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both statement-I and statement-II are correct and statement-II explains statement-I.
Statement-I is incorrect, but statement-II is correct.
Both statement-I and statement-II are correct, but statement-II does not explain statement-I.
Statement-I is correct, but statement-II is incorrect.
questions.e: The 2025-26 budget allocated 11.21 lakh crore (3.1% of GDP) to capex. Capex has a high multiplier effect (up to 4.8 in the long term), which justifies the increased allocation to boost the economy.

questions.q: Q.50) Consider the following statements: Statement I: A central bank's decision to cut its policy interest rate is an effective tool against demand-pull inflation. Statement II: Deflationary tendencies in an economy prompt an expansionary monetary policy stance to stimulate demand. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement-I is incorrect, but statement-II is correct.
Both statement-I and statement-II are correct, but statement-II does not explain statement-I.
Statement-I is correct, but statement-II is incorrect.
Both statement-I and statement-II are correct and statement-II explains statement-I.
questions.e: Statement I is incorrect because cutting interest rates worsens inflation; rates must be increased. Statement II is correct as expansionary policy (lower rates) helps counter deflation by stimulating demand.

questions.q: Q.51) Consider the following statements: Statement I: The Eastern Ghats are a discontinuous range of mountains. Statement II: The Eastern Ghats are older than the Western Ghats and are heavily eroded by rivers. Which of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both statement-I and statement-II are correct and statement-II explains statement-I.
Statement-I is incorrect, but statement-II is correct.
Statement-I is correct, but statement-II is incorrect.
Both statement-I and statement-II are correct, but statement-II does not explain statement-I.
questions.e: The Eastern Ghats are discontinuous because they are older geologically and have been significantly eroded by the major rivers of South India like the Godavari and Krishna.

questions.q: Q.52) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Baratang 2️⃣ Great Nicobar 3️⃣ Middle Andaman 4️⃣ Little Andaman. Arrange the following islands of the Andaman & Nicobar group from North to South:
questions.e: The correct sequence from North to South is Middle Andaman, followed by Baratang, then Little Andaman, and finally Great Nicobar.

questions.q: Q.53) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Egypt 2️⃣ Eritrea 3️⃣ Jordan 4️⃣ Saudi Arabia 5️⃣ Syria. How many of the above countries border the Red Sea?
questions.e: Egypt, Eritrea, Jordan (via Gulf of Aqaba), and Saudi Arabia all border the Red Sea. Syria is a Mediterranean littoral state and does not border the Red Sea.

questions.q: Q.54) Consider the following statements: Statement-I: Water vapour acts as a feedback rather than as primary driver of current global warming. Statement-II: Climate forcings initiate global warming, while feedbacks amplify it. Statement-III: Water vapour concentration depends on temperature set by non-condensable gases, not vice versa. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of the Statements-II and III is correct and that explains Statement-I
questions.e: Water vapor is a feedback because its concentration is determined by the warming initiated by non-condensable forcings like CO2. It amplifies the initial warming, creating a positive feedback loop.

questions.q: Q.55) As one moves from west to east, which one of the following is the correct sequence of cities?
questions.e: Longitude-wise, Rome is at 12.5°E, Cairo at 31°E, Moscow at 37.6°E, and Beijing at 116.4°E.

questions.q: Q.56) With reference to the sugarcane industry, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The recovery rate of sugar from cane is generally higher in tropical regions compared to subtropical regions of India. 2️⃣ Uttar Pradesh ranks highest in India in ethanol production due to its dominance in sugarcane acreage. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct as tropical climates favor higher sucrose accumulation. Statement 2 is incorrect; while UP has the most acreage, Maharashtra often leads in ethanol production due to higher distillery capacity.

questions.q: Q.57) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ mRNA vaccines deliver genetic instructions to human cells to produce specific antigenic proteins. 2️⃣ Conjugate vaccines are designed to enhance immune responses against weak polysaccharide antigens. 3️⃣ Pathogens in live attenuated vaccines cannot replicate inside the host. How many of the statements given are not correct?
questions.e: Statement 3 is incorrect because live attenuated vaccines contain weakened pathogens that *can* replicate inside the host to induce long-lasting immunity. Statements 1 and 2 are correct.

questions.q: Q.58) Consider the following statements with reference to cement production in India: 1️⃣ India is the largest cement producer in the world. 2️⃣ Gypsum is added during manufacturing to control the setting time of cement. 3️⃣ Portland Pozzolana Cement (PPC) uses fly ash from thermal power plants to reduce carbon dioxide emissions. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect as India is the second-largest producer after China. Statements 2 and 3 are correct regarding the use of gypsum for setting time and fly ash in PPC.

questions.q: Q.59) With reference to satellite-based augmentation systems (SBAS), consider the following: 1️⃣ They improve the positional accuracy of Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) signals. 2️⃣ They can support drone navigation and vessel traffic management. 3️⃣ India's GAGAN and Japan's MSAS Satellite Augmentation System are examples of SBAS. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All statements are correct. SBAS improves accuracy for multisectoral use, and GAGAN and MSAS are regional examples of such systems.

questions.q: Q.60) Consider the following statements with regard to recent global on Artificial Intelligence (AI) regulation: 1️⃣ The EU Artificial Intelligence Act adopts a comprehensive risk-based regulatory framework. 2️⃣ The OECD AI Principles emphasise human-centred values and are legally binding on all member countries. 3️⃣ The United Nations High-Level Advisory Body on Al has proposed a global governance framework to address cross-border risks posed by advanced Al systems. How many of the statements given above are not correct?
questions.e: Statement 2 is not correct as the OECD AI Principles are voluntary and non-binding. Statements 1 and 3 correctly describe the EU's risk-based approach and the UN's governance proposals.

questions.q: Q.61) Consider the following statements with regard to rare earth element magnets: 1️⃣ Neodymium-Iron-Boron (NdFeB) magnets are the strongest commercially available permanent magnets and are widely used in wind turbines and electric vehicles. 2️⃣ Samarium-Cobalt (SmCo) magnets are highly resistant to demagnetisation at high temperatures but are less strong than NdFeB magnets. How many of the statements given above are not correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. NdFeB magnets are the strongest, while SmCo magnets offer better temperature stability, making them suitable for high-heat applications.

questions.q: Q.62) With reference to the application of space technology, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The International Space Station (ISS) and Tiangong Space Station are modular orbital platforms designed for long-term habitation and research. 2️⃣ The SpaceX Dragon capsule is a reusable spacecraft designed for transporting crew and cargo. 3️⃣ Tiangong Space Station and the SpaceX Dragon capsule both support autonomous docking with ISS in Low Earth Orbit. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect as China's Tiangong Space Station is not compatible with the ISS docking system and cannot dock with it.

questions.q: Q.63) With reference to types of nanomaterials, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Nanocomposites often combine nanoparticles with bulk materials to enhance mechanical and thermal properties. 2️⃣ Graphene are three-dimensional carbon sheets with weak tensile strength but superior compressive strength. 3️⃣ Fullerenes are a class of carbon-based nanomaterials in which carbon atoms are arranged in a closed-cage structure. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect as Graphene is a two-dimensional sheet with extremely high tensile strength.

questions.q: Q.64) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Lentil 2️⃣ Bengal gram 3️⃣ Sesbania 4️⃣ Mustard 5️⃣ Jowar. How many of the above belong to the Fabaceae family, known for their nitrogen-fixing ability?
questions.e: Lentil, Bengal gram, and Sesbania are part of the Fabaceae (legume) family. Mustard is from the Brassicaceae family, and Jowar (Sorghum) is from the Poaceae family.

questions.q: Q.65) With reference to power sources for spacecraft, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Some spacecraft use radioisotope sources to generate heat and electricity. 2️⃣ Solar panels become less efficient as the distance from the Sun increases. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. Deep-space missions use radioisotope generators because solar panel efficiency drops significantly (inverse-square law) as distance from the Sun increases.

questions.q: Q.66) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Supernova explosions often lead to the formation of neutron stars or black holes. 2️⃣ White dwarfs can undergo further nuclear fusion reactions after their formation. 3️⃣ A white dwarf in a close binary system can explode as a supernova if it reaches the Chandrasekhar limit. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because white dwarfs are stellar remnants that no longer support nuclear fusion; they gradually cool over time.

questions.q: Q.67) In the human body, which one of the following functions is associated with histamine?
o: Generation of electrical impulses in cardiac tissue
questions.e: Histamine is primarily involved in initiating inflammatory and allergic responses, causing vasodilation and increased vascular permeability.

questions.q: Q.68) The Monroe Doctrine, recently discussed in the media, is related to:
o: The collective security mechanism under the United Nations Charter
The principle of non-alignment adopted by newly independent countries during the Cold War
The policy of economic sanctions imposed through multilaterally international institutions
The assertion of a regional sphere of influence by the United States in the Western Hemisphere
questions.e: The 1823 Monroe Doctrine asserted that the Western Hemisphere was closed to European intervention, establishing a U.S. sphere of influence in the Americas.

questions.q: Q.69) With reference to the Sixth Schedule in the Constitution of India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Its provisions apply to the administration of the tribal areas in the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. 2️⃣ If there are different Scheduled Tribes in an autonomous district, the District Magistrate can divide the area into autonomous regions. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the power to divide an autonomous district into autonomous regions rests with the Governor, not the District Magistrate.

questions.q: Q.70) Which one of the following authority is vested with power to create new Ministries or Departments at the Union level in India?
questions.e: New ministries and departments are created by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister under the Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961.

questions.q: Q.71) In the context of Indian Polity, the 'Mavalankar Rule' is related to which one of the following?
o: The minimum quorum required to conduct the business of the House
The procedure for the election of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The protocol for the Speaker to cast a deciding vote only in the case of a tie
Recognizing a party for the purpose of designating the Leader of the Opposition
questions.e: The Mavalankar Rule established the requirement that a party must have at least 10% of the House's strength to be recognized as an official opposition party.

questions.q: Q.72) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Creation of a new All-India Services 2️⃣ Authorising the Parliament to legislate on a subject in the State List 3️⃣ Selection of Cabinet Ministers 4️⃣ Initiate a motion for the removal of the Vice-President. How many of the above are the exclusive powers of Rajya Sabha?
questions.e: Creation of All-India Services (Art. 312), legislating on State List (Art. 249), and initiating removal of the VP (Art. 67b) are exclusive powers. Selection of Cabinet Ministers is not exclusive as they can come from either House.

questions.q: Q.73) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The total membership of a State Legislative Council cannot be less than 40, or more than one-third of the total membership in the Legislative Assembly. 2️⃣ Parliament through a constitutional amendment can enact a law for either abolition or creation of Legislative Council in a State. 3️⃣ The area of territorial constituencies for election of members of a Legislative Council are decided by the Parliament. 4️⃣ The Chairman of a Legislative Council can participate in the proceedings of the House when a resolution for his removal is under consideration. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 2 is incorrect because such a law is passed by simple majority and is not considered a constitutional amendment under Article 368. Statements 1, 3, and 4 are correct.

questions.q: Q.74) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ First state created on a linguistic basis—Andhra Pradesh 2️⃣ First state to implement the Panchayati Raj system—Rajasthan 3️⃣ First State to implement comprehensive land reforms—Kerala. How many of the pairs given above are correct?
questions.e: All three pairs are historically correct. Andhra was the first linguistic state , Rajasthan inaugurated Panchayati Raj , and Kerala implemented major land reforms.

questions.q: Q.75) With reference to the Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It provides for establishment of CAMPA funds under the Public Accounts of India and Public Accounts of each State. 2️⃣ Under the fund-sharing mechanism, the State Governments are entitled to receive a minimum 50% of the fund to ensure ecological restoration. 3️⃣ User agencies are responsible for undertaking and maintaining compensatory afforestration for the first five years. 4️⃣ The 'Net Present Value' is a mandatory charge to compensate for the loss of forest ecosystem services. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 2 is incorrect as States receive 90% of the funds. Statement 3 is incorrect as the State government, not the user agency, performs the afforestation work. Statements 1 and 4 are correct.

questions.q: Q.76) With reference to the National Water Development Agency (NWDA), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is an autonomous society functioning under the Ministry of Jal Shakti. 2️⃣ Its primary mandate is to prepare Detailed Project Reports for the inter-linking of Peninsular and Himalayan rivers. 3️⃣ The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 empowers it to regulate the development and management of groundwater resources in the country. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 3 is incorrect because the power to regulate groundwater rests with the Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA). Statements 1 and 2 are correct.

questions.q: Q.77) Consider the following statements with reference to payment architecture in India: 1️⃣ The Payments Regulatory Board is a statutory regulatory body chaired by the Minister of Finance. 2️⃣ The National Payments Corporation of India regulates the online retail payment systems in India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect as the PRB is chaired by the Governor of the RBI. Statement 2 is incorrect as NPCI is an operational body that *operates* systems like UPI, while the RBI performs the regulatory role.

questions.q: Q.78) The term 'Engels' Pause,' sometimes seen in the news, refers to which one of the following?
o: It refers to an economic paradox where worker wages stagnated despite significant growth in labor productivity.
It denotes a stagnation in manufacturing productivity due to the depletion of non-renewable resources.
It refers to a cyclical stagnation in productivity growth observed after the peak of a long-wave economic cycle.
It is a government policy of halting wage increases to allow capitalists to accumulate the necessary funds for industrial expansion.
questions.e: Engels' Pause describes the lag in real wage growth despite rising productivity during the Industrial Revolution, leading to increased inequality.

questions.q: Q.79) With reference to Indian economy, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ A Preference Share holder has a claim on dividends before an equity share holder and enjoys voting rights proportional to their holding. 2️⃣ Unlike Equity Shares, debentures represent a part ownership in the company and carry voting rights for the holder. 3️⃣ The holder of an Equity Share has the lowest claim on the company's assets and income, typically receiving the residual profit after liquidation. 4️⃣ A Warrant is a long-term option issued by a company that gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to purchase a specific number of shares at a predetermined price. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect as preference shares generally do not have voting rights. Statement 2 is incorrect as debentures are debt instruments and do not carry voting rights. Statements 3 and 4 are correct.

questions.q: Q.80) 'Investment Project Financing and Development Policy Financing' are the primary lending instruments of:
questions.e: IPF and DPF are the two main lending mechanisms of the World Bank (specifically IBRD and IDA) to support projects and policy reforms.

questions.q: Q.81) Which one of the following international organizations recently launched the 'Global Alliance Against Hunger and Poverty'?
questions.e: The alliance was officially launched at the G20 Leaders' Summit in 2024 to eliminate hunger by 2030.

questions.q: Q.82) With reference to the 'Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PMDDKY)', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It aims to strengthen productivity, improve irrigation efficiency, and modernize post-harvest management in the select 100 districts. 2️⃣ Under the scheme district-level plans will be prepared by the union Ministry of Agriculture with technical support from Indian Council of Agricultural Research. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the plans (DADP) are prepared at the district level by Samitis led by District Collectors, not the Union Ministry.

questions.q: Q.83) Consider the following actions by the Government: 1️⃣ Increase in Revenue expenditure 2️⃣ Decreasing public expenditure 3️⃣ Increase in corporate tax rate 4️⃣ Reducing subsidies. How many of the above given measures taken by the government are classified as contractionary fiscal measures?
questions.e: Decreasing expenditure, increasing taxes, and reducing subsidies pull money out of the economy, making them contractionary. Increase in revenue expenditure is expansionary.

questions.q: Q.84) With reference to the Indian Public Finance consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The proportion of long-term external debt of India is higher than its short-term maturity debt. 2️⃣ Interest payments constitute the single largest component of the union government's revenue expenditure. 3️⃣ Under the new fiscal roadmap as outlined in the budget of 2025-26, the Union Government aims to bring down its debt to GDP ratio to 50% by 2031. 4️⃣ Multilateral organizations and bilateral individual countries are the largest external debt creditors of India. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 4 is incorrect because commercial lenders are India's largest external creditors (39.6%). Statements 1, 2, and 3 are correct.

questions.q: Q.85) Consider the following statements: The effect of depreciation of a currency is that it generally: 1️⃣ Increases inflation in the domestic market. 2️⃣ Decrease the competitiveness of the domestic exports in the foreign markets. 3️⃣ Cause higher cost of servicing external commercial borrowings. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct (imported inflation). Statement 2 is incorrect because depreciation *increases* export competitiveness. Statement 3 is correct as more domestic currency is needed to pay back foreign-denominated loans.

questions.q: Q.86) Consider the following statements with regard to the market equilibrium in an economy: 1️⃣ In a competitive market, equilibrium is attained at a price where there is no tendency for change as the quantity demanded equals quantity supplied. 2️⃣ Consumer equilibrium is a situation where the consumer maximises total utility given income and prices, even though consumption may still change with variations in income or prices. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. Market equilibrium occurs when supply equals demand, and consumer equilibrium is the point of maximum satisfaction relative to budget constraints.

questions.q: Q.87) Consider the following information: 1️⃣ Chola—Vanji—Puhar 2️⃣ Chera—Uraiyur—Musiri 3️⃣ Pandya—Madurai—Korkai. In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
questions.e: Row 1 is incorrect (Chola capital was Uraiyur). Row 2 is incorrect (Chera capital was Vanji). Row 3 is correct (Pandya capital was Madurai and port was Korkai).

questions.q: Q.88) Which one of the following periods of ancient history witnessed the literary developments in grammar, marked by works such as Ashtadhyayi, Mahabhashya and Amarakosa?
questions.e: While Panini (Ashtadhyayi) was earlier, the Gupta age saw the critical study and consolidation of these works, along with the composition of the Amarakosa.

questions.q: Q.89) With regard to the architectural contributions of the Pala dynasty, consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Gopala—Vikramshila monastery 2️⃣ Dharmapala—Somapuri monastery 3️⃣ Mahipala I—Odantapuri monastery. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only Pair 2 is correct. Vikramshila was established by Dharmapala (not Gopala), and Odantapuri was established by Gopala (not Mahipala I).

questions.q: Q.90) With reference to developments in the 18th century India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The decline of the Mughal Empire led to the emergence of several regional states that exercised de facto sovereignty while formally acknowledging Mughal authority. 2️⃣ Indian merchants and bankers played an important role in financing regional states and facilitating inland and overseas trade. 3️⃣ European trading companies completely replaced Indian merchants in both internal and external trade during this period. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because Indian merchants continued to dominate internal trade and collaborate in external trade throughout the 18th century.

questions.q: Q.91) With reference to the evolution of local government in India during British rule, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Lord Ripon's Resolution of 1882 emphasised decentralisation, financial autonomy, and greater participation of Indians in local bodies. 2️⃣ Local bodies under British rule were primarily created to promote democratic self-governance rather than administrative efficiency. 3️⃣ The Government of India Act, 1935 strengthened provincial control over local governments while expanding their scope and functions. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect as the primary motive was administrative efficiency and financial relief for the colonial state, not true democratic self-governance.

questions.q: Q.92) With reference to peasant movements in the second half of the 19th century, consider the following statements: Statement I: They were primarily directed against oppressive revenue systems and exploitative intermediaries rather than against British rule as a whole. Statement II: Colonial land revenue arrangements intensified peasant indebtedness, eviction, and economic insecurity. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.e: Agrarian distress caused by colonial revenue policies led to revolts focused on immediate exploiters like zamindars and moneylenders rather than the overall colonial structure.

questions.q: Q.93) Consider the following information: 1️⃣ Social Service League—Narayan Malhar Joshi—To demand better conditions of life and work 2️⃣ Indian National Social Conference—Mahadev Govind Ranade—To oppose kulinism and polygamy 3️⃣ Nishkam Karma Math—Debendranath Tagore—To promote inter caste marriages. In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
questions.e: Rows 1 and 2 are correct. Row 3 is incorrect as Nishkam Karma Math was founded by Dhondo Keshav Karve, not Debendranath Tagore, and worked for women's education.

questions.q: Q.94) With reference to Mahatma Gandhi, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ He believed that non-violence (Ahimsa) was a practical tool for political action and mass mobilisation. 2️⃣ He considered modern industrial civilisation as inherently exploitative and advocated a village-based self-sufficient economy. 3️⃣ He emphasised the concept of Trusteeship to resolve conflicts between capital and labour without abolishing private property. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three statements accurately reflect Gandhian philosophy on political action, economics, and social harmony.

questions.q: Q.95) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Rivers in the Himalayan region and the Indo-Gangetic plains have been identified as highly vulnerable to reservoir sedimentation. Statement II: Himalayan rivers carry high sediment loads due to steep gradients and active erosion, while rivers of the Indo-Gangetic plains depend largely on natural river flows with limited reservoir-based regulation. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.e: High sediment loads and limited regulation make these regions' reservoirs highly susceptible to siltation and capacity loss.

questions.q: Q.96) Consider the following statements with regard to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972: 1️⃣ Wild animals listed in Schedule I can be hunted if they pose a danger to human life only with the permission of the Chief Wildlife Warden. 2️⃣ The Central Government can declare any wild animal as vermin by placing it in Schedule V. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Act excludes Schedule I and Part II of Schedule II animals from being declared as vermin.

questions.q: Q.97) The Dry Sorbent Injection and Wet Limestone Scrubbing techniques, sometimes seen in the news, are associated with:
o: removal of sulphur dioxide (SO2) from flue gases in thermal power plants
control of particulate matter in urban air pollution
reduction of nitrogen oxides (NOx) emissions from automobiles
questions.e: DSI and Wet Limestone Scrubbing are Flue Gas Desulphurisation (FGD) technologies used to control SO2 emissions in thermal plants.

questions.q: Q.98) Consider the following statements with regard to the Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) framework: 1️⃣ It ensures that benefits derived from the use of biological resources and associated traditional knowledge are fairly and equitably shared with local communities. 2️⃣ The funds under the ABS framework are released under the provisions of Biological Diversity Act, 2002 by the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA). 3️⃣ Traditional knowledge used in dairy farming, animal husbandry and bee keeping are covered under the ABS framework. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect as traditional practices in dairy and animal husbandry are specifically excluded from the ABS framework's definition of commercial utilization.

questions.q: Q.99) With regard to the Ramsar sites in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ All the seven north-eastern States have at least one Ramsar site. 2️⃣ All the States in southern India have at least one Ramsar site. 3️⃣ All the Union Territories located in northern India have at least one Ramsar site. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All statements are incorrect. In the NE, Arunachal, Meghalaya, and Nagaland have no sites. In the South, Telangana has no sites. In northern UTs, Delhi and Chandigarh have no sites.

questions.q: Q.100) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Humpback whale—Keystone species 2️⃣ Horn- eyed ghost crab—Bubble netting hunting technique 3️⃣ Hoolock gibbon—Only ape found in india. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 3 is correct. Pair 1 is incorrect as bubble-netting is a technique used by whales, and pair 2 is incorrect as the ghost crab is a keystone species, not a bubble-netter.

questions.q: Q.1) If India introduces horizontal reservation for transgender persons within existing SC/ST/OBC quotas to address their intersectional vulnerabilities. This policy best represents:
questions.e: The introduction of horizontal reservation for transgender persons aims to address intersectional disadvantages and reflects distributive justice. Distributive justice is concerned with the fair distribution of social goods and opportunities such as education, jobs, and political representation. It requires special measures for those who are structurally disadvantaged.

questions.q: Q.2) Consider the following statements with regard to Tribunals in India: 1️⃣ Tribunals constituted under Article 323B are confined to the subject matters expressly enumerated in that Article. 2️⃣ The secretarial staff of both Houses of Parliament comes under the jurisdiction of the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT). 3️⃣ Foreigners Tribunals are quasi-judicial bodies constituted by the Ministry of External Affairs. Which of the statements given above are not correct?
questions.e: The list in Article 323B is illustrative, not exhaustive. Members of the secretarial staff of Parliament are expressly excluded from CAT's jurisdiction. Foreigners Tribunals are constituted by the Ministry of Home Affairs, not the Ministry of External Affairs.

questions.q: Q.3) Consider the following statements with regard to the Lok Adalats: 1️⃣ They do not have jurisdiction over offences which are non-compoundable under any law. 2️⃣ The Permanent Lok Adalat (PLA) has a pecuniary jurisdiction of up to 10 lakh for disputes involving Public Utility Services. 3️⃣ Unlike regular Lok Adalats, which handle pre-litigation matters, a PLA can only take up cases already pending in a court. 4️⃣ A party cannot make an appeal to any court against the award made by a Lok Adalat. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Lok Adalats have no jurisdiction over non-compoundable offences. The pecuniary jurisdiction of PLA was enhanced to 1 crore in 2015. PLAs deal only with pre-litigation disputes, whereas regular Lok Adalats handle both pending and pre-litigation cases.

questions.q: Q.4) Consider the following statements with regard to the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023: 1️⃣ It explicitly defines and penalises 'mob lynching'. 2️⃣ It provides for the conduct of a trial in absentia for proclaimed offenders. 3️⃣ It mandates that a trial court must deliver its judgment within 90 days of the completion of arguments. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Mob lynching is defined in the BNS, not the procedural BNSS. The BNSS introduces trial in absentia for proclaimed offenders who evade trial. It mandates judgment delivery within 30 days of completion of arguments, extendable to 45 days.

questions.q: Q.5) With regard to the amendment to the Constitution of India, consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ 24th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971: Provided that Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution 2️⃣ 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003: Introduced limits on the size of the Council of Ministers at the Union and State levels 3️⃣ 105th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2021: Provided reservation for the economically weaker sections 4️⃣ 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023: Empowered States to prepare their own lists of Socially and Economically Backward Classes. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. The 105th Amendment restored the power of States to maintain their own SEBC lists, while the 103rd Amendment provided for EWS reservation. The 106th Amendment  provides 33% reservation for women in legislatures.

questions.q: Q.6) Consider the following statements with regard to the membership of the Parliament of India: 1️⃣ A person elected to both the Lok Sabha and a State Legislature must resign the State Legislature seat within 14 days, failing which the Lok Sabha seat becomes vacant. 2️⃣ If an independent member joins any political party after the expiry of six months, s/he is disqualified. 3️⃣ As per the Representation of the People Act, 1951, if a person is detained under a preventive detention law, he is disqualified from being a Member of Parliament. How many of the statements given above are not correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct per the Prohibition of Simultaneous Membership Rules. Statement 2 is incorrect because an independent member is disqualified if they join a party at any time. Statement 3 is incorrect because preventive detention is not a ground for disqualification under the RPA 1951.

questions.q: Q.7) Consider the following statements with reference to Article 25 of the Constitution of India: 1️⃣ It guarantees the freedom of religion to both individuals and religious denominations. 2️⃣ It covers religious practices but does not cover religious doctrines. 3️⃣ It is available to both citizens and non-citizens. 4️⃣ It is subject to restrictions of morality and health. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 25 guarantees rights to individuals, while Article 26 covers religious denominations. It covers both religious beliefs (doctrines) and practices. It is available to all persons (citizens and non-citizens) and is subject to public order, morality, and health.

questions.q: Q.8) Which of the following are valid constitutional or statutory routes for the removal of a Chief Minister of a State in India? 1️⃣ By the Governor, when the Chief Minister loses the confidence of the State Legislative Assembly 2️⃣ By the President of India, upon the proclamation of a National Emergency under Article 352 3️⃣ By the Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly, through disqualification under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution of India 4️⃣ By the Governor, if the Chief Minister fails to become a member of the State Legislature within six months of appointment. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: A CM is removed if they lose the majority in the Assembly or fail to secure a seat in the legislature within six months. National Emergency (Art 352) does not lead to the dismissal of the state government. Disqualification by the Speaker creates a vacancy but is not a direct "removal" route from the CM post.

questions.q: Q.9) In the 2026 General Elections, a candidate for the Lok Sabha uses their personal social media handle to post a video where a prominent religious leader "blesses" the candidate and warns followers that voting for any other candidate would be a "spiritual sin." The rival candidate challenges the election results in the High Court. Based on the principles of Indian democracy and established judicial precedents, how is the Court likely to interpret this scenario?
o: The election is valid because the appeal was made through a personal social media account and not through a formal religious institution or official campaign office.
The election is valid because the religious leader is an independent citizen with a Fundamental Right to Freedom of Speech under Article 19(
The election is valid provided the candidate did not personally pay the religious leader, as "Corrupt Practice" under RPA, 1951 requires a direct financial transaction or bribery.

The election is void because using "spiritual pressure" to interfere with the free exercise of a voter's choice constitutes "Undue Influence" under Section 123 of the Representation of the People Act (RPA), 1951.
questions.e: Section 123 of the RPA 1951 defines "undue influence" to include the use of spiritual threats or moral pressure to interfere with a voter's choice. Equating a voting choice with a "spiritual sin" violates the requirement for free and fair elections.

questions.q: Q.10) When the Reserve Bank of India purchases government securities from the public, which of the following will definitely increase immediately?
questions.e: RBI purchases inject liquidity. M0 (Reserve Money) increases as bankers' deposits with RBI rise. M3 (Broad Money) increases because the sellers receive payments as bank deposits. M1 is not "definitely" affected because payments could be credited to time deposits.

questions.q: Q.11) With regard to the Index of Eight Core Industries, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The current base year for calculating the index is 2022-23. 2️⃣ Among the eight core industries, crude oil has the highest weight, while cement has the lowest weight. 3️⃣ The overall year-on-year growth rate of the Index has remained positive in the last ten years except during 2020-21. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The base year is 2011-12. Refinery products have the highest weight (28.04%), and fertilizers have the lowest (2.63%). The index contracted only in 2020-21 due to the pandemic.

questions.q: Q.12) Consider the following scenarios: 1️⃣ Excess aggregate demand in the economy 2️⃣ Credit expansion leading to higher consumption 3️⃣ Increase in fuel and food prices due to supply shocks 4️⃣ Disruptions in global supply chains 5️⃣ Structural deficiencies in agricultural marketing and logistics. In how many of the cases given above is monetary policy likely to be effective in directly controlling inflation?
questions.e: Monetary policy is effective against demand-side inflation (scenarios 1 and 2). It is largely ineffective against supply-side shocks, global chain disruptions, or structural market deficiencies (scenarios 3, 4, and 5).

questions.q: Q.13) With regard to the presence of foreign banks in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ India follows the principles of reciprocity and single mode of presence with respect to foreign banks. 2️⃣ As per India's WTO commitments, foreign banks may open up to 12 branches annually. 3️⃣ Automatic expansion is restricted if foreign banks' capital and reserves in India exceed 20% of the total Indian banking system. Which of the statements given is/are above are correct?
questions.e: India uses "reciprocity" and "single mode of presence" (WOS or branch). WTO commitments allow 12 branches per year. Expansion is restricted if foreign banks' capital/reserves exceed 20% of the system to maintain financial stability.

questions.q: Q.14) With reference to the inflation in the economy, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ There is an inverse relationship between inflation rates and the market price of existing fixed-rate bonds. 2️⃣ High inflation generally reduces the real value of the government's outstanding liabilities. 3️⃣ Under a floating exchange rate system, high domestic inflation typically leads to appreciation of the domestic currency. How many of the statements give above are correct?
questions.e: Inflation leads to higher interest rates, which lowers the price of existing bonds. It erodes the real value of fixed-rate debt, helping the government. High inflation usually leads to currency depreciation, not appreciation.

questions.q: Q.15) Consider the following statements: Statement I: If the Indian Rupee depreciates against the US Dollar, India's export competitiveness will always increase. Statement II: The Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER) adjusts the nominal exchange rate for inflation differentials between India and its major trading partners. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.e: Depreciation does not always increase competitiveness if domestic inflation is very high or global demand is weak. REER is a better measure of competitiveness as it adjusts for inflation differences.

questions.q: Q.16) A decrease in the Weighted Average Call Rate (WACR) indicates:
o: a decrease in the borrowing cost for the banks
an increase in the borrowing cost for banks
decrease in long-term interest rates in the economy
an increase in liquidity deficit in the banking system
questions.e: WACR is the rate at which banks lend/borrow overnight funds. A decrease in WACR reflects easier liquidity conditions and lower short-term borrowing costs for banks.

questions.q: Q.17) With reference to the Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) policy in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Proposal for FDI under the Government route is examined and approved by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT). 2️⃣ FDI proposals involving an amount exceeding 500 crore require approval of the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA). 3️⃣ Over the past five years, India has consistently remained among the top three recipients of global FDI inflows. Which of the statements given above are not correct?
questions.e: Government route proposals are approved by concerned Ministries, with DPIIT as a facilitator. CCEA approval is needed for proposals above 5,000 crore. India was 15th in FDI inflows in 2024, not in the top three.

questions.q: Q.18) Consider the following statements with regard to the rapeseed-mustard in India: 1️⃣ It is a notified oilseed for which the Government announces Minimum Support Price (MSP). 2️⃣ It is predominantly cultivated as a Rabi oilseed crop in India. 3️⃣ Its oil is primarily used for industrial purposes. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Rapeseed-mustard is a notified oilseed under MSP. It is a major Rabi crop harvested in Feb-March. Its oil is primarily used for edible purposes (cooking, pickling), not industrial purposes.

questions.q: Q.19) Consider the following statements with regard to the Brown Forest Soil: 1️⃣ In India, it is predominantly found in the Deccan Plateau region. 2️⃣ It is rich in organic matter and humus. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Brown forest soils (mountain soils) are found in high-elevation regions like the Himalayas and Ghats. The Deccan Plateau is characterized by black (regur) soil. These forest soils are rich in organic matter from leaf decomposition.

questions.q: Q.20) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Between 40 N and 40 S latitudes, incoming insolation exceeds outgoing terrestrial radiation. Statement II: The atmosphere is primarily heated by long-wave radiation emitted by the Earth's surface. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: Statement I is correct: the tropical/subtropical zone has an energy surplus. Statement II is correct: the atmosphere is heated from below by terrestrial radiation. However, Statement II describes the heating mechanism but does not explain the latitudinal energy imbalance.

questions.q: Q.21) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Thrust: Main Himalayan System 2️⃣ Strike-Slip: San Andreas Fault 3️⃣ Normal: Bhuj Fault in Kachchh. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Thrust faults are common in the Himalayas (collision zone). The San Andreas is a classic strike-slip fault. The Bhuj Fault is a reverse/compressional fault, not a normal fault.

questions.q: Q.22) Which of the following is/are directly responsible for the initiation of the Thermohaline Circulation in oceans? 1️⃣ High sea-surface temperatures in tropical oceans 2️⃣ Sea ice formation in polar regions 3️⃣ Strong equatorial upwelling driven by trade winds. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Thermohaline circulation is driven by density differences. In polar regions, sea ice formation expels salt, increasing density and causing water to sink. High tropical temperatures keep water buoyant, preventing sinking. Upwelling involves rising water, not the sinking needed to initiate the "conveyor belt."

questions.q: Q.23) Consider the following countries: 1️⃣ Algeria 2️⃣ Mali 3️⃣ Burkina Faso 4️⃣ Ghana. How many of the above are crossed by both the Tropic of Cancer and the Prime Meridian?
questions.e: The Tropic of Cancer and Prime Meridian cross simultaneously only in two countries: Algeria and Mali.

questions.q: Q.24) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Mohenjo-daro: Ravi 2️⃣ Sanchi Stupa: Betwa 3️⃣ Amaravati Stupa: Godavari 4️⃣ Ajanta Caves: Moosi. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Mohenjo-daro is on the Indus (Harappa is on the Ravi). Sanchi is near the Betwa. Amaravati is on the Krishna. Ajanta is on the Waghora River. Only pair II is correct.

questions.q: Q.25) The Northern Indian Ocean lacks a permanent circular gyre system as found in the Atlantic and the Pacific Oceans. Which one of the following best explains the reason behind this?
o: There is no anti-cyclonic circulation of ocean currents in the Indian Ocean
The Indian Ocean has monsoon drift that causes a seasonal reversal in the wind direction
The Coriolis force is too weak in the Indian Ocean region
The Indian Ocean remains under the permanent influence of the Westerlies throughout the year
questions.e: The northern Indian Ocean is affected by monsoonal winds which seasonally change direction. This leads to a reversal of ocean currents (clockwise in summer, counterclockwise in winter), preventing a permanent gyre.

questions.q: Q.26) Which of the following best describes the concept of permaculture?
o: Designing human settlements and agricultural systems that mimic the patterns and relationships found in nature
Promoting large-scale monoculture to ensure global food security
Maximizing crop yield through the intensive use of chemical fertilizers
Developing genetically modified seeds that are resistant to all pests
questions.e: Permaculture is an ethical design approach that mimics natural ecosystems (biodiversity, layered vegetation, nutrient cycles) to create sustainable, self-sufficient systems.

questions.q: Q.27) Which one of the following statements is not correct with regard to the Government of India Act, 1919?
o: It introduced a limited franchise, under which certain women were granted the right to vote for the first time.
It empowered the Governor to resume the administration of transferred subjects in the event of a breakdown of the constitutional machinery within the province.
It introduced diarchy in the provinces, dividing subjects into reserved and transferred categories.
It introduced bicameralism in the provincial legislatures.
questions.e: The Act of 1919 introduced bicameralism at the Central level, but provincial legislatures remained unicameral. It did introduce diarchy in provinces and a limited franchise that included some women.

questions.q: Q.28) The Piprahwa Relics, discovered in 1898 by British engineer William C. Peppe, were found at the Piprahwa Stupa, which is located at the site widely identified as?
questions.e: The Piprahwa Relics are associated with Kapilavastu, the ancient capital of the Shakyas where Siddhartha Gautama spent his early life. Kushinagar is where Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana.

questions.q: Q.29) Consider the following information: 1️⃣ Treaty of Tordesillas: Spain and Portugal - Divided the newly discovered world between Spain and Portugal 2️⃣ Treaty of Alinagar: British East India Company and Nawab of Bengal - Restored British trading privileges 3️⃣ Treaty of Allahabad: British East India Company and Mughal Emperor - Granted Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the British 4️⃣ Treaty of Sugauli: British East India Company and Nepal - Defined Nepal's boundaries and allowed a British Resident in Kathmandu 5️⃣ Treaty of Pondicherry: British East India Company and France - Brought an end to the Second Carnatic War. In which of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
o: I, II, III, IV and V
II, III, IV and V only
questions.e: All five rows are correct. The Treaty of Tordesillas divided global expansion between Spain and Portugal. Alinagar followed the capture of Calcutta. Allahabad established British Diwani. Sugauli ended the Anglo-Nepalese war. Pondicherry ended the Second Carnatic War.

questions.q: Q.30) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Strachey Commission: Famine measure 2️⃣ Raleigh Commission: University Education 3️⃣ Whitley Commission: Labour conditions 4️⃣ Hilton Young Commission: Relations with Princely States 5️⃣ Chatfield Commission: Agriculture. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Strachey (Famine), Raleigh (Universities), and Whitley (Labour) are correct. Hilton Young Commission  was on currency/finance (led to RBI), and Chatfield Commission  was on Indian defence.

questions.q: Q.31) Which one of the following is not one of the 'Three Universal Truths' in Buddhist philosophy?
o: Relativity and multiplicity of truth, where multiple viewpoints can all be partially correct
The soul is non-eternal and non-permanent in nature
Sorrow is intrinsic to human existence
The world is transient and constantly changing
questions.e: The "Three Marks of Existence" (Tilakkhana) are Anicca (Impermanence), Anatta (No-soul), and Dukkha (Suffering). Relativity of truth (Anekantavada) is a fundamental doctrine of Jainism, not Buddhism.

questions.q: Q.32) Arrange the following types of pottery in India in chronological order of their origin: 1️⃣ Painted Grey Ware 2️⃣ Northern Black Polished Ware 3️⃣ Rouletted ware 4️⃣ Glazed ware. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: PGW (c. 1100-500 BCE) was followed by NBPW (c. 700 BCE onwards). Rouletted ware is Early Historic (c. 500 BC - 200 AD). Glazed ware became prominent in India around the 12th century AD with Arab influence.

questions.q: Q.33) With reference to "antiquity", under the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act, 1972, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Any manuscript to be considered an antiquity should be in existence for not less than seventy five years. 2️⃣ An article must have been in existence for not less than one hundred years to be declared an antiquity. 3️⃣ The Act explicitly declares sacred temple sculptures to be living entities. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under the 1972 Act, manuscripts must be at least 75 years old, while other objects must be at least 100 years old. The Act does not recognize sculptures as living entities; its focus is regulation and preservation.

questions.q: Q.34) With reference to the chronology and features of the Indus Valley Civilisation, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Rakhigarhi and Banawali exhibit a continuous sequence across the Early, Mature, and Late Harappan phases. 2️⃣ Extensive stone-based fortifications and a tripartite town plan are distinctive features of Dholavira. 3️⃣ Kalibangan reached its maximum urban extent and significance during the Late Harappan phase. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Rakhigarhi and Banawali show evolutionary continuity. Dholavira is known for its stone walls and three-part layout (Citadel, Middle, Lower). Kalibangan peaked in the Mature phase and was largely abandoned before the Late phase.

questions.q: Q.35) In the context of recent technological developments in India, what are 'DHRUV64' and 'THEJAS64'?
o: GPS-aided navigation systems for the Indian Navy
Advanced stealth variants of the Dhruv Utility Helicopter and Tejas Fighter Jet
Linux-based operating systems designed for secure government communications
Microprocessors capable of handling strategic operations and industrial automation
questions.e: DHRUV64 and THEJAS64 are indigenously developed microprocessors (based on RISC-V) developed by C-DAC for strategic operations, industrial automation, and space systems.

questions.q: Q.36) With reference to nanobodies, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They can be used as antivenoms and are much smaller, simpler, and more stable than conventional antibodies. 2️⃣ They are found naturally in camelids and some cartilaginous fish. 3️⃣ Unlike conventional antibodies, they cannot be mass produced in bacterial cell culture. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Nanobodies are single-domain antibodies found in camels and sharks. They are stable and small. Unlike conventional antibodies, they *can* be easily mass-produced in bacteria like E. coli.

questions.q: Q.37) Consider the following statements: Statement I: All genetic codons in all living organisms code for the same amino acids. Statement II: Genetic codons are read during the process of translation to determine the order of amino acids in a protein. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both statement I and statement II are correct and statement II explains statement I.
Statement I is incorrect, but statement II is correct.
Statement I is correct, but statement II is
Both statement I and statement-II are correct, but statement II does not explain statement I.
questions.e: The genetic code is *nearly* universal, but there are rare variations (e.g., in human mitochondria), so Statement I is incorrect. Statement II accurately describes translation.

questions.q: Q.38) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Check the health and chlorophyll of plants content. 2️⃣ Track pollution or harmful algal blooms in water bodies. 3️⃣ Detects underground oil and gas deposits even in the absence of surface seepage. 4️⃣ Determine the exact chemical composition of deep ocean water at all depths. How many of the statements given above are applications of remote sensing satellites?
questions.e: Remote sensing can check plant health (chlorophyll) and track water pollution/algal blooms. However, sensors cannot see through the Earth's crust or miles of deep ocean water directly; they only detect surface anomalies.

questions.q: Q.39) With reference to the Quantum technology, consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Scrambling: Dispersal of local information across all the other quantum bits 2️⃣ Interference: Subatomic particles interact with and influence themselves and other particles 3️⃣ Quantum advantage: Performing a task that is beyond the reach of traditional supercomputers. In how many of the above rows is the information correctly matched?
questions.e: Scrambling refers to information spreading across entangled qubits. Interference is a wave-like interaction. Quantum advantage is when quantum computers outperform classical ones for specific tasks.

questions.q: Q.40) With with regards to gravitational lensing, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It occurs when a massive celestial body causes a curvature of spacetime leading the path of light to bend. 2️⃣ It can occur only when the source, the lens, and the observer are perfectly aligned along a straight line. 3️⃣ It can be used to directly detect gravitational waves through spacetime distortions. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Gravitational lensing is caused by spacetime curvature. Perfect alignment is not necessary (though it creates Einstein rings). It is used to detect distant objects but not for the direct detection of gravitational waves (done by LIGO/Virgo).

questions.q: Q.41) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Significantly enhancing data storage capacity in hard drives 2️⃣ Facilitating energy efficient electronics by controlling electron spin 3️⃣ Making nonvolatile memory that retains data without continuous power. How many of the above are the potential applications of Altermagnetism?
questions.e: Altermagnetism (zero net magnetization) allows for denser data storage. It enables spin-polarized currents for spintronics (energy efficiency) and is used for non-volatile memory that holds data without power.

questions.q: Q.42) Consider the following organelles: 1️⃣ Mitochondria 2️⃣ Nucleus 3️⃣ Chloroplast 4️⃣ Nitroplast. How many of the above possess a double membrane and contain their own genetic material (DNA)?
questions.e: Mitochondria, Nucleus, and Chloroplasts are well-known double-membraned organelles with DNA. The Nitroplast, a recently discovered nitrogen-fixing organelle in marine algae, also follows this pattern.

questions.q: Q.43) Consider the following processes: 1️⃣ Steam Methane Reforming 2️⃣ Partial Oxidation 3️⃣ Autothermal Reforming 4️⃣ Gasification. How many of the above processes can be used to produce syngas?
questions.e: All four processes—SMR (natural gas + steam), Partial Oxidation (hydrocarbon + limited oxygen), ATR (combined), and Gasification (solid fuels)—produce syngas (H2 and CO).

questions.q: Q.44) Consider the following statements with regard to nitrous oxide: 1️⃣ Globally, agricultural use of nitrogen based fertilizers constitutes the largest anthropogenic source of its emissions. 2️⃣ It is the most significant ozone layer depleting substance being emitted into the atmosphere. 3️⃣ It is approximately 270 times more potent than carbon dioxide in terms of warming the planet. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Fertilizer use is the top human source of N2O. It is currently the most significant ozone depleter and is ~273 times more potent than CO2 as a greenhouse gas.

questions.q: Q.45) Consider the following countries: 1️⃣ Peru 2️⃣ Colombia 3️⃣ Venezuela 4️⃣ Ecuador 5️⃣ Bolivia 6️⃣ Chile. How many of the above share the Amazon rainforest?
questions.e: The Amazon spans Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Bolivia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Guyana, Suriname, and French Guiana. Chile does not contain any part of the Amazon.

questions.q: Q.46) Consider the following ecological/evolutionary factors: 1️⃣ Mutation 2️⃣ Abundance of resources 3️⃣ Continuous gene flow 4️⃣ Reproductive isolation. How many of the above factors are responsible for speciation?
questions.e: Mutation (source of divergence) and Reproductive isolation (barrier to gene flow) are key to speciation. Abundance of resources leads to stability, while continuous gene flow prevents divergence by keeping the gene pool unified.

questions.q: Q.47) "These microscopic, single-celled organisms are found in diverse aquatic environments ranging from oceans to freshwater lakes. Characterized by unique cell walls made of silica, they exhibit an extraordinary variety of intricate shapes and patterns. They serve as the bedrock of aquatic food webs and are prolific producers, accounting for nearly 25% of the Earth's total oxygen production." The above description best refers to which one of the following?
questions.e: Diatoms are single-celled algae with silica shells (frustules). They account for ~25% of global oxygen and are the foundation of aquatic food webs.

questions.q: Q.48) Recently, the vast brown seaweed known as the 'Great Atlantic Sargassum Belt (GASB)' was in the news. In this context, which of the following is not a factor contributing to this phenomenon?
o: Anthropogenic nutrient enrichment like phosphorus and nitrogen from agricultural runoff.
Strengthening of cold, oxygen-rich upwelling currents.
Fine dust blown from the Sahara Desert enriching the ocean with iron.
Anomalous rise in sea surface temperatures.
questions.e: Sargassum growth is fueled by nutrients from runoff, iron from Sahara dust, and warm temperatures. It is associated with *warmer* currents, not cold upwelling currents.

questions.q: Q.49) With reference to the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)'s Global Forest Resources Assessment 2025, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Brazil has the largest area under tropical forests in the world. 2️⃣ Among continents, only Asia recorded an increase in forest area between 1990 and 2025. 3️⃣ India recorded the highest annual net gain in tropical forest area. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Brazil has the largest tropical forest area. Asia is the only region with net forest area growth (due to China and India). However, China recorded the highest annual net gain, not India.

questions.q: Q.50) With reference to rangelands, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They collectively account for more than half of the Earth's terrestrial surface. 2️⃣ They store a greater proportion of carbon below ground compared to forest ecosystems. 3️⃣ The United Nations has designated 2026 as the International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists.
