Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Rangelands cover over 50% of Earth's land. They store more carbon below ground (roots/soil), making them stable sinks. 2026 is indeed the IYRP.

questions.q: Q.51) Consider the following statements with regard to the Indian polity: 1️⃣ In matters in the Concurrent List where Parliament has legislated, executive power vests exclusively in the Union Government. 2️⃣ The President of India may entrust Union executive functions to a State with the consent of the State Government. 3️⃣ Parliament can confer Union legislative powers on States through legislation. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: For concurrent subjects, executive power typically rests with states unless specifically conferred on the Union. Under Art 258, the President can entrust functions with state consent. Parliament cannot transfer its exclusive legislative competence to states by ordinary law.

questions.q: Q.52) With reference to the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Article 131 of the Constitution of India empowers the Supreme Court to decide inter-governmental disputes involving questions of law only. 2️⃣ It extends to disputes between the Union and a Public Sector Undertaking (PSU). 3️⃣ It extends to disputes arising out of any pre-Constitution treaty, agreement, or covenant. 4️⃣ It extends to the adjustment of certain expenses and pensions between the Centre and the States. Which of the statements given above is/are not correct?
questions.e: Art 131 covers law *and* fact. PSUs are not federal units. Pre-constitutional treaties and financial adjustments (expenses/pensions) are specifically excluded from Art 131 jurisdiction.

questions.q: Q.53) In which of the following matters is the Legislative Council placed on an unequal footing with the Legislative Assembly in India? 1️⃣ Approval of Ordinances issued by the Governor 2️⃣ Participation in the discussion on the State Budget 3️⃣ Ratification of a Constitutional Amendment Bill 4️⃣ Moving or passing a No-Confidence Motion against the Council of Ministers, when the Chief Minister is a member of the Legislative Council 5️⃣ Enlargement of the jurisdiction of the State Public Service Commission. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: I, II, III, IV and V
questions.e: The Council and Assembly are equal for Ordinances, Budget discussion, and SPSC jurisdiction. They are unequal for Money Bills, No-Confidence motions (CM responsibility), and Constitutional Amendment ratification.

questions.q: Q.54) The President of India's power to make regulations for the "peace, progress and good government" of certain Union Territories is subject to which of the following conditions?
o: It can be exercised for Puducherry only when its Legislative Assembly is dissolved or suspended.
It is a discretionary power not requiring the advice of the Union Council of Ministers.
It can be used to repeal or amend any Act of Parliament applicable to the Union Territory.
questions.e: The President can regulate UTs like Ladakh and Lakshadweep. For Puducherry, this applies only during Assembly suspension. These regulations can amend Parliamentary Acts. This is not a discretionary power.

questions.q: Q.55) With reference to the Finance Commission of India (FCI), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is a quasi-judicial body whose recommendations are binding on the Union Government to maintain fiscal federalism. 2️⃣ The qualifications of the Chairman and members of the Commission are determined by the Parliament. 3️⃣ Income Distance has historically carried the highest weight in the horizontal devolution formula to promote fiscal equalisation among States. 4️⃣ The Sixteenth Finance Commission has been tasked with reviewing the present arrangements for financing Disaster Management initiatives. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: FC recommendations are advisory (not binding). Parliament determines detailed qualifications (Act of 1951). Income Distance had a 45% weight in the 15th FC. The 16th FC is reviewing disaster financing.

questions.q: Q.56) Consider the following offences: 1️⃣ Offences related to human trafficking 2️⃣ Offences related to prohibited arms under the Arms Act, 1959 3️⃣ Cyber-terrorism and offences under the Explosive Substances Act, 1908 4️⃣ Investigation of offences committed against Indian citizens or Indian interests outside India 5️⃣ Economic offences involving bank fraud and money laundering 6️⃣ Offences relating to taxation and customs duty evasion. How many of the above fall within the jurisdiction of the National Investigation Agency (NIA)?
questions.e: NIA covers terrorism, human trafficking, prohibited arms, and crimes against Indian interests abroad (Points 1-4). Standard bank frauds (Point 5) and taxation/customs crimes (Point 6) fall under other agencies like CBI, ED, or SFIO.

questions.q: Q.57) With reference to the Constitution of India, consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Part II: Citizenship 2️⃣ Part XI: Relations between the Union and the States 3️⃣ Part XVI: Special Provisions relating to Certain Classes 4️⃣ Part XX: Official language. Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Part II (Citizenship), Part XI (Union-State relations), and Part XVI (Special provisions) are correct. Part XX deals with Amendment of the Constitution, while Part XVII deals with Official Language.

questions.q: Q.58) Consider the following statements: Statement I: The provisions of Part IXB of the Constitution of India relating to State Cooperative Societies were struck down by the Supreme Court of India. Statement II: Cooperative societies fall exclusively within the State List in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.e: Statement I is correct (SC struck down Part IXB for state cooperatives due to procedural errors). Statement II is incorrect because while State cooperatives are in the State List, *Multi-State* cooperatives fall in the Union List.

questions.q: Q.59) Consider the following statements with regard to the qualifications for election as President of India: 1️⃣ He must be at least twenty-five years old. 2️⃣ He must be a citizen of India by birth. 3️⃣ He must be qualified to be elected as a member of the Lok Sabha. 4️⃣ A sitting Vice-President is eligible to contest the election for the office. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The President must be 35 years old (not 25) and a citizen of India (not necessarily by birth). Statements 3 and 4 are correct: qualification for Lok Sabha is required, and sitting VPs do not hold an "office of profit" for contest purposes.

questions.q: Q.60) Consider the following statements with regard to the Four Labour Codes in India: 1️⃣ The definition of wages has been standardised across labour codes. 2️⃣ Aggregators are required to contribute 4-5% of their annual turnover to a social security fund for gig and platform workers. 3️⃣ A trade union must secure at least 75% worker membership to be recognised as the sole negotiating union. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Wages have a uniform definition across codes. Aggregators contribute 1-2% of turnover (capped at 5% of worker payments). A union needs 51% (not 75%) membership to be the sole negotiator.

questions.q: Q.61) Consider the following statements with regard to the PM-SETU Scheme: 1️⃣ It is a Central Sector Scheme. 2️⃣ It is primarily aimed at the upgradation of the Government Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs). 3️⃣ It will be implemented through the public-private partnership (PPP) model. 4️⃣ It has financial support from the Asian Development Bank and the World Bank. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PM-SETU is a Centrally *Sponsored* Scheme (outlay shared with states). It upgrades 1,000 ITIs via a PPP model. It is co-financed by the ADB and World Bank.

questions.q: Q.62) With reference to the Payments Regulatory Board, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is a six-member body that has replaced the Board for Regulation and Supervision of Payment and Settlement Systems (BPSS). 2️⃣ The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India is the ex officio Chairman of this Board. 3️⃣ It is legally mandated to meet at least four times in a financial year. 4️⃣ It is responsible for the regulation of both electronic and non-electronic payment systems. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The PRB replaced BPSS and is chaired by the RBI Governor. It must meet at least *twice* (not four times) a year. It regulates all payment systems, including non-electronic ones.

questions.q: Q.63) With reference to the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies of the World Trade Organization, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It recognises the principle of Special and Differential Treatment for developing and least developed countries. 2️⃣ It excludes aquaculture and inland fisheries from its scope. 3️⃣ A Fish Fund has been established to provide financial assistance exclusively to the least developed countries for implementing the agreement. 4️⃣ India has ratified this agreement. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Fish Fund provides assistance to *both* developing and LDCs. India has not yet ratified the agreement (process is ongoing).

questions.q: Q.64) With reference to India's foreign trade, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The total annual value of exports from India has steadily increased between 2014-15 and 2024-25. 2️⃣ In 2024-25, the share of the services sector in India's total exports is higher than that of merchandise exports. 3️⃣ The engineering goods sector constitutes the largest component of India's merchandise exports. 4️⃣ The Export Promotion Mission focuses on tariff-impacted sectors and non-traditional districts. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Total exports fluctuated during the decade (not steady). Merchandise exports ($437B) remain higher than services ($387B). Engineering goods is the top merchandise component (26.67%). EPM focuses on specific sectors and non-traditional districts.

questions.q: Q.65) With reference to the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It defines the term 'essential commodities'. 2️⃣ Both the Central and State Governments can add or remove commodities from the list of essential commodities in public interest. 3️⃣ Fertilisers and petroleum products are not covered under the Act. Which of the statements given above are not correct?
questions.e: The Act does not define "essential commodities"; it only authorizes the Center to declare them. Only the Central Government can add/remove items. Fertilizers and petroleum products *are* covered under the Act.

questions.q: Q.66) Consider the following items: 1️⃣ Research and Development (R&D) expenditure 2️⃣ Mailing list of clients 3️⃣ Acquisition of specialized manufacturing robots 4️⃣ Undeveloped land. How many of the above are considered Intangible Investments?
questions.e: R&D and client mailing lists have no physical form but provide value, making them intangible. Robots and undeveloped land are physical, tangible assets.

questions.q: Q.67) Consider the following statements with regard to the Yamuna River: 1️⃣ It originates from the Yamunotri Glacier in the Garhwal Himalayas. 2️⃣ It flows through Uttarakhand, Haryana, Delhi, and Uttar Pradesh only. 3️⃣ The catchment area of the river accounts for around two-fifths of the Ganga River basin. 4️⃣ The Tons River, originating from the Bandarpunch Glacier, is its largest tributary. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Yamuna rises at Yamunotri. It also briefly touches Himachal Pradesh (Statement 2 is wrong). It accounts for 2/5ths of the Ganga basin and its largest tributary is the Tons.

questions.q: Q.68) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Darjeeling: Himachal Himalayas 2️⃣ Male Mahadeshwara: Vindhya Range 3️⃣ Kalvarayan: Eastern Ghats 4️⃣ Rajgir: Chota Nagpur Plateau. How many of the pairs given above are correct?
questions.e: Darjeeling is in the Lesser (Himachal) Himalayas. Kalvarayan is in the Eastern Ghats. Rajgir is an extension of the Chota Nagpur Plateau. MM Hills are in the Eastern Ghats, not the Vindhya Range.

questions.q: Q.69) With regard to nuclear energy in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Nuclear power contributes less than 5% to India's total electricity generation. 2️⃣ India has set a target of achieving 30 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2031-32. 3️⃣ Natural uranium is the primary fuel used in India's present nuclear power reactors. 4️⃣ The Tummalapalle uranium belt in Andhra Pradesh is the largest known uranium reserve in India. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Nuclear power is ~3% of the mix. The target for 2031-32 is ~22.48 GW. Most Indian PHWRs use natural uranium. Tummalapalle is the largest domestic reserve.

questions.q: Q.70) Consider the following information: 1️⃣ Vanadium: Highest Reserves in China, Highest Reserves in India-Arunachal Pradesh, Primary use-High-strength steel and aerospace alloys 2️⃣ Graphite: Highest Reserves in China, Highest Reserves in India-Jharkhand, Primary use-Refractory materials and lithium-ion batteries 3️⃣ Nickel: Highest Reserves in Indonesia, Highest Reserves in India-Odisha, Primary use-Stainless steel production 4️⃣ Tungsten: Highest Reserves in Australia, Highest Reserves in India-Andhra Pradesh, Primary use-Cutting tools and electrical applications. In how many of the above rows is the information correctly matched?
questions.e: Rows 1 and 3 are correct. For Graphite, Arunachal Pradesh has the largest reserves (not Jharkhand). For Tungsten, China has the largest global reserves (not Australia) and Karnataka has the largest Indian resources.

questions.q: Q.71) Which of the following statements correctly distinguish between the Tropical Cyclones and the Extra-Tropical Cyclones? 1️⃣ Tropical cyclones possess a distinct frontal system, whereas extra-tropical cyclones are driven by thermal convection. 2️⃣ While the extra-tropical cyclones originate over both land and sea, the tropical cyclone can originate only over the sea. 3️⃣ Tropical cyclones generally move from east to west, while extra-tropical cyclones move from west to east. 4️⃣ Extra-tropical cyclones are usually more destructive and affect a much smaller area than tropical cyclones. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Extra-tropical cyclones have frontal systems; tropical ones don't. Tropical cyclones only form over sea. Tropical ones move East to West (Trade winds), while Extra-tropical ones move West to East (Westerlies). Tropical ones are more destructive but smaller.

questions.q: Q.72) Consider the following statements with regard to the atmospheric humidity: 1️⃣ The Relative Humidity of air does not change with temperature as long as the total amount of moisture remains constant. 2️⃣ The Dew Point is the temperature that a parcel of air would reach if all the water vapor in the air parcel were condensed. 3️⃣ The latent heat is released into the air when the water vapour is condensed into water droplets. 4️⃣ The wet-bulb temperature is the lowest air temperature that can be achieved by evaporating water from the air. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Relative humidity changes with temperature (higher temp lowers RH). Dew point is the saturation temperature, not the point of total condensation. Statements 3 and 4 correctly describe latent heat release and wet-bulb temperature.

questions.q: Q.73) Which of the following forces is/are currently recognised by geologists as the primary cause for the movement of tectonic plates? 1️⃣ Mantle convection 2️⃣ Ridge push 3️⃣ Tidal force 4️⃣ Polar-fleeing force 5️⃣ Slab pull. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: I, II, III and V only
questions.e: Mantle convection, Ridge push, and Slab pull are primary drivers. Tidal and Polar-fleeing forces (suggested by Wegener) are not considered significant causes of plate motion today.

questions.q: Q.74) Consider the following information: 1️⃣ Esker: Glacier - Deposition 2️⃣ Yardang: Wind - Deposition 3️⃣ Loess: Oceanic Waves - Erosion 4️⃣ Uvala: Ground Water - Erosion. In how many of the above rows is the information correctly matched?
questions.e: Eskers are glacial depositional features. Uvalas are groundwater erosional features. Yardangs are wind *erosional* features. Loess is wind *depositional*.

questions.q: Q.75) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Volcanic dust reflects microwaves effectively, making it easily detectable on standard weather radar. 2️⃣ LIDAR systems are ineffective at detecting volcanic ash due to the presence of glass-rich silicate particles in it. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Volcanic ash is too small to reflect microwaves well, so it's missed by weather radar. LIDAR is actually *highly* effective because laser light interacts strongly with the glass-rich silicate in ash.

questions.q: Q.76) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Integrated Drone Detection & Interdiction System (IDD&IS): Micro-rockets and micro-missiles 2️⃣ Bhargavastra: Electronic jamming and Laser-based neutralisation 3️⃣ Indrajaal: Al-enabled detection, jamming and spoofing 4️⃣ D4 Anti-Drone System: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS). How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: IDD&IS uses laser neutralisation (Hard-kill) and jamming. Bhargavastra uses micro-rockets and missiles. Indrajaal (AI patrol) and D4 (DRDO system using GNSS/jamming) are correctly matched.

questions.q: Q.77) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Biologics are complex, large-molecule drugs produced using living organisms or their biological components. 2️⃣ Biosimilars are identical drugs derived from non-biological sources and match the reference biologic exactly in structure, safety, and efficacy. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Biologics are large molecules from living systems. Biosimilars are highly similar but *not* identical, and they must also come from biological sources (not non-biological).

questions.q: Q.78) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Microwaves can penetrate through clouds, dust and rain to reveal the Earth's surface. Statement II: Microwaves have shorter wavelengths and higher energy compared to visible and infrared radiation. Which of the following is correct with respect to the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.e: Statement I is correct: long microwaves pass through atmospheric interference. Statement II is incorrect: microwaves have *longer* wavelengths and *lower* energy than visible/IR light.

questions.q: Q.79) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Conduct electricity only along its edges. 2️⃣ Efficiently convert heat into electricity at the nanoscale. 3️⃣ Be a safer alternative to lead in quantum dots. How many of the above are properties and applications of bismuth metal in its 2D state?
questions.e: In 2D form, bismuth acts as a topological insulator (edge conduction). It has strong thermoelectric properties for heat conversion and is being explored as a non-toxic alternative to lead in quantum dots.

questions.q: Q.80) Which of the following hormones are primarily responsible for promoting growth in plants? 1️⃣ Auxins 2️⃣ Gibberellins 3️⃣ Cytokinins 4️⃣ Ethylene 5️⃣ Abscisic Acid. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: I, II, III and IV only
questions.e: Auxins, Gibberellins, and Cytokinins are primary growth promoters. Ethylene (ripening) and Abscisic Acid (stress/dormancy) often inhibit growth.

questions.q: Q.81) With reference to India's "Environmental Accounting on Forests, 2025", consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It shows an increase in provisioning and regulating services over the last decade. 2️⃣ It follows the UN System of Environmental- Economic Accounting (SEEA) framework. 3️⃣ It was released by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC). Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2025 account shows increased ecosystem services and uses the UN SEEA framework. It was released by MoSPI, not MoEFCC.

questions.q: Q.82) Consider the following pollutants: 1️⃣ Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAHs) 2️⃣ Dioxins 3️⃣ Mercury 4️⃣ Furans 5️⃣ Sulphur dioxide. How many of the above are direct byproducts of plastic production or degradation?
questions.e: Burning or degrading plastics releases PAHs, Dioxins, and Furans. Mercury and Sulphur dioxide come from other sources like coal burning and smelting.

questions.q: Q.83) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Polar bears are found only in the Arctic Circle. 2️⃣ No species of penguins are found north of the Equator. 3️⃣ Some coral species are found in the Arctic Circle. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Polar bears are Arctic-exclusive. The Galápagos penguin lives at the equator and some individuals cross north. Cold-water corals (like Lophelia) thrive in Arctic waters.

questions.q: Q.84) Which one of the following reproduces asexually through vegetative propagation using tubers, producing genetically identical offspring (clones), and at the same time, it can reproduce sexually through flowers and seeds, leading to genetic variation in offspring?
questions.e: Potato uses tubers (modified stems) for asexual cloning. It also flowers and produces seeds for sexual reproduction. Onion uses bulbs; Turmeric and Ginger use rhizomes.

questions.q: Q.85) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Pin Valley National Park 2️⃣ Chandratal wetland 3️⃣ Sarchu Wildlife Sanctuary 4️⃣ Pangong Tso Lake 5️⃣ Kibber Wildlife Sanctuary. How many of the above constitute the Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve?
questions.e: Pin Valley, Chandratal, Sarchu, and Kibber are in Himachal Pradesh and part of the reserve. Pangong Tso is in Ladakh and is not part of this specific Himachal-based reserve.

questions.q: Q.86) With reference to the Kyoto Protocol, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is the only global climate treaty that imposed legally binding greenhouse gas emission reduction targets exclusively on developed countries. 2️⃣ The Clean Development Mechanism enabled developed countries to meet part of their emission reduction targets by funding mitigation projects in developing countries. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Kyoto  mandated targets only for Annex I (developed) nations. The CDM was a key flexibility mechanism allowing them to earn credits via projects in developing countries.

questions.q: Q.87) With reference to the Greenhouse Gas Emission Intensity Target Rules, 2025, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It sets 2023-24 as the baseline to reduce emission intensity. 2️⃣ It allows eligible industries to trade excess reductions as carbon credits. 3️⃣ It authorizes the Bureau of Energy Efficiency to impose penalties for non-compliance. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2025 rules use 2023-24 as the baseline and allow carbon credit trading. While BEE determines credits, enforcement/penalties are handled by environmental authorities like CPCB.

questions.q: Q.88) Consider the following information: 1️⃣ Keoladeo National Park: Rajasthan - Man-made wetland 2️⃣ Gokul Reservoir: Gujarat - Coastal wetland 3️⃣ Kopra Jalashay: Bihar - Oxbow lake 4️⃣ Lonar Lake: Maharashtra - Crater formed in basaltic rock of the Deccan Traps. In how many of the above rows is the information correctly matched?
questions.e: Keoladeo (Rajasthan/Man-made) and Lonar (Maharashtra/Meteorite crater) are correct. Gokul Reservoir is in Bihar (Oxbow). Kopra Jalashay is in Chhattisgarh (Man-made).

questions.q: Q.89) Consider the following statements: Statement I: Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) can be used as a method to capture atmospheric carbon dioxide. Statement II: Elements like calcium and magnesium released upon weathering of rock react with carbonic acid to produce limestone. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: ERW speeds up the natural process where rocks react with CO2. Statement II correctly explains the chemical mechanism (calcium/magnesium + CO2 = limestone) that captures the carbon.

questions.q: Q.90) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Drop-in biomaterials: Chemically identical to petroleum-derived materials 2️⃣ Drop-out biomaterials: Chemically similar to conventional plastics 3️⃣ Novel biomaterials: Possess self-healing materials or bioactive implants. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Drop-in materials (like bio-PET) are chemically identical. Novel materials have new properties like self-healing. Drop-out materials (like PLA) are chemically *distinct* (not similar) and need different processing.

questions.q: Q.91) With reference to the inscriptional evidence of the Gupta period consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They present us evidence that the Guptas and the Vakatakas of the Deccan were contemporaries. 2️⃣ No woman was allowed to possess independent access to resources such as land. 3️⃣ Agrahara lands were not to be entered by soldiers and policemen and were exempted from major and minor taxes. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Inscriptions confirm the Gupta-Vakataka link (e.g., marriage of Prabhavatigupta). Although legal texts restricted women, inscriptional evidence (Poona copper plates) shows elite women like Prabhavatigupta *did* grant and own land. Agrahara grants provided fiscal/administrative immunity.

questions.q: Q.92) Which of the following Sangam era texts provides a detailed genealogy and record of the achievements of the Chera kings?
questions.e: Patitrupathu (one of the Eight Anthologies) is dedicated to Chera history. Purananuru covers all three dynasties. Tolkappiyam is a grammar text. Maduraikanchi achievement of the Pandya king.

questions.q: Q.93) With regard to classical languages in India, which of the following statements are not correct? 1️⃣ Classical language status is accorded by the Ministry of Culture based on prescribed criteria reflecting cultural significance. 2️⃣ One of the eligibility conditions, for classical status, requires a high antiquity of early literature or recorded history spanning about 1,500-2,000 years. 3️⃣ Pali and Prakrit were the first two languages to receive Classical status. 4️⃣ All languages recognised as Classical are included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Tamil was the first classical language . Pali and Prakrit were added in 2024 and are *not* currently in the Eighth Schedule.

questions.q: Q.94) Consider the following statements with reference to the Ellora caves: 1️⃣ It includes the 'Teen Tal', a three-storeyed cave structure associated with a major Buddhist monastic complex. 2️⃣ The Kailasa Temple is the largest monolithic rock-cut temple in the world. 3️⃣ Most of the Brahmanical and Jain caves at Ellora are attributed to the Rashtrakuta rulers. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: 'Teen Tal' is a Buddhist cave. Kailasa is the world's largest monolithic structure. While Buddhist/Brahmanical caves are Rashtrakuta-linked, the Jain caves post-date them (Kalyani Chalukyas/Yadavas).

questions.q: Q.95) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Alexander Cunningham: The Bhilsa Topes 2️⃣ Alfred Foucher: The Monuments of Sanchi 3️⃣ Colin Mackenzie: A Forgotten Empire: Vijayanagar. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Cunningham wrote *The Bhilsa Topes*. Foucher (with Marshall) wrote *The Monuments of Sanchi*. *A Forgotten Empire* was written by Robert Sewell (Mackenzie only surveyed the ruins).

questions.q: Q.96) In 1922, Mahatma Gandhi was arrested on charges of sedition for:
o: Articles in Young India, particularly "Tampering with Loyalty"
Speeches at the Indian National Congress session
questions.e: Gandhi was arrested in March 1922 for three articles in *Young India*, including "Tampering with Loyalty," where he preached disaffection against the government.

questions.q: Q.97) With reference to the Bengal British India Society, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It was established by members of the Young Bengal movement with the support of George Thompson. 2️⃣ It functioned as a platform in India for radical advocacy against social and religious orthodoxies. 3️⃣ It actively participated in the Revolt of 1857. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Established in 1843, it was a platform for radical/liberal reform inspired by the Young Bengal movement. It did not participate in the 1857 military rebellion.

questions.q: Q.98) The abolition of 'cowrie' currency and the requirement of revenue payment in silver were the primary economic triggers for which early anti-British resistance?
questions.e: The Paika Rebellion  in Odisha was triggered by grievances over land policies, the abolition of cowrie currency, and the high price of salt under British rule.

questions.q: Q.99) Decision Tree and Random Forest, sometimes seen in the news, are related to:
o: Machine learning algorithms for data analysis and predictions
questions.e: Decision Tree and Random Forest are machine learning algorithms used to analyze patterns and make predictions (e.g., crop recommendations based on data).

questions.q: Q.100) With reference to Gopalhari Deshmukh 'Lokahitawadi', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ He served as a judge under the British administration while contributing to social reform through his writings. 2️⃣ He advocated for the reorganization of Indian society based on rational principles and secular values. 3️⃣ He was the founder of the periodical Sudharak, which primarily spoke against untouchability. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Deshmukh was a British-era judge and rationalist reformer. The periodical *Sudharak* was founded by Gopal Ganesh Agarkar, not Lokahitawadi.
